Real Sociedad, based in San Sebastián, finished third in Spain’s top division last term behind Real Madrid and Barcelona. The qualifying draw was split into two sections, with a “champions path” for winners of their domestic divisions drawn separately to the “league path” which contained domestic runners-up and third-placed sides such as Chelsea.

Køge, who eliminated the Scottish champions Hearts earlier in the qualification process, were pitted against PSV Eindhoven, while the most eye-catching tie of the round will see Ajax take on Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Liverpool told to sign £60m-rated defender offered to Chelsea and Manchester United
Sports.content:
Liverpool should sign Myles Lewis-Skelly to compete with Milos Kerkez at left-back.

That's the view of Peterborough United owner and Reds fan Darragh MacAnthony amid uncertainty over the 19-year-old's Arsenal future.



4 Lewis-Skelly faces an uncertain future at boyhood club Arsenal Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that Lewis-Skelly has been offered to other Premier League clubs including rivals Manchester United and Chelsea.

The news comes after Arsenal completed the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle last week.

Although he has mostly played as a left-back, Lewis-Skelly is a midfielder by trade throughout his senior Arsenal career.



However, Guimaraes has joined strong midfield competition in Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino.

Lewis-Skelly made just five Premier League starts last season, and a move away may therefore offer more minutes from the off.



How much is Lewis-Skelly worth?

Reacting to the news on talkSPORT with Max Scott, MacAnthony said: "I love him, I think he's a great, young player."

"Why has he not been offered to Liverpool?" he asked, before adding: "Someone said, 'What's he worth?'



"I said, 'Anywhere from £40-60million for a player of that age that's English.'"

Scott then asked MacAnthony if he would welcome Lewis-Skelly at Liverpool this summer.

Kerkez is set to be the first-choice left-back in the new season ahead of Kostas Tsimikas, who is understood to want to fight for his place.

4 MacAnthony would love to see Liverpool make a move for Lewis-Skelly Credit: Getty



4 He wants the club to bring in competition for Kerkez Credit: Getty

"All day long," MacAnthony said: "We need competition for our left-back. No disrespect to Tsimikas, but not for me. And, he can play in midfield, we've seen him play in that role in midfield..."

When it was suggested that Lewis-Skelly's strongest position is in midfield, despite his experience at left-back, he replied: "Correct.

"Liverpool are crying out for that type of player who's got those defensive skills but also still has, technically, the attacking ability as well."



What could Lewis-Skelly be thinking?

Lewis-Skelly has been at Arsenal since the age of eight and worked through the academy ranks to feature in the first team.

He has already made 75 senior appearances for the north Londoners and won a Premier League title.

Whilst an exit is certainly not confirmed with Guimaraes' arrival, it does raise questions over whether or not he has a place in the team.

4 Lewis-Skelly has been praised for his versatility on the pitch Credit: Getty



"I know that you look at the game from the perspective of an owner and a businessman, and you can sometimes, sort of, remove yourself from the emotion of the game, and understandably so," Scott said to MacAnthony.

"But if you're Myles Lewis-Skelly, an Arsenal fan brought through the academy, you proved yourself last season, broke back into the team, been an integral part, and now you're hearing you're offered to other Premier League clubs...

"Is that just the ruthlessness of the game, or can you understand he might be frustrated by it?"

"I don't know where the report has come from, but I would imagine the player and his agent would know," MacAnthony responded. "So, they'd be aware, I'm sure this hasn't come out as a surprise on them.



"Maybe he wants to play more football, how many times did he play last year? I know he was in the Champions League final, I know he played a good few games at the end of the season.

"Maybe at that age, 19, 20, they want to go Man United and they want to go and play every week. We know United need that type of player, there's no doubt about it.

"They were in for (Lewis) Hall at Newcastle, I think the price of that was probably too expensive.

"This is a young, English talent who will be in the England team for years to come, so it's sensible business for whoever gets him."

Sports.title: Man United urged to go all-in for Premier League defender who wants to leave club
Sports.content:
Man United urged to go all-in for Premier League defender who wants to leave club

Djed Spence to Manchester United?

It’s a no-brainer according to Manchester United fan and talkSPORT host Flex.

4 Spence is being courted by Inter Milan but should Man United be in for the England man? Credit: Getty



The Tottenham defender was among England’s standout performers at the World Cup despite garnering detractors over his inclusion in Thomas Tuchel’s 26-man squad.

The 26-year-old silenced the doubters with a host of superb displays during the Three Lions’ run to the semi-finals.

But despite his heroics in North America, Spence’s future at Tottenham is unclear with the player understood to be open to a move away from the club.

Serie A champions Inter have been long-standing admirers of the full-back.



talkSPORT reported on Tuesday that the Nerrazzuri had reopened talks with Tottenham over signing him.

However, what may come as a surprise to many is the projected fee of around £25-30million that could see Spence land in Milan.



Spurs have spent heavily this summer with over £200m splashed on reinforcements and the club’s transfer record smashed twice in the same window.

Therefore, the north London club may need to offload some talents to balance the books and Spence could be at the top of the list.



A good fit at Old Trafford?

But Flex is hoping Inter won’t have an easy path to obtaining Spence’s signature and admits that Manchester United would benefit from the star’s skill set.

“This is one we need to be all over,” he told talkSPORT.

4 Spence was in sensational form for England at the World Cup Credit: Getty

“I’m sorry, we need to raise our ceiling of players we need to choose from.

“Not everyone has to be the number one starter or the left-back or right-back for the next ten years. You can’t always sign that player.



“But for where we are and the depths of the competitions we want to go into, stylistically I need different options.”

Conceding defeat

Flex was more than happy to take his own dose of humble pie after watching Spence’s World Cup performances.

“Djed Spence, I gave him a rough time. I’ll hold my hands up,” he added.

“Going into the World Cup when he was in the squad and there was no Trent [Alexander -Arnold] and no Lewis Hall and I saw people like Dan Burn and Djed Spence, I was like ‘what is this?’



4 Spence could be available for just £30m this summer Credit: Getty

“But he bit down on his gum shield and said I’m here to show people what I’m about. He didn’t play too dissimilar to how he actually plays.

“He’s very good in 1v1 situations, he’s extremely quick and can play on both sides.

“You’re talking about value in the market, I’d absolutely have him for £25million.”



Flex admits that a move for the Tottenham star might split the fan base but says that he could be prove to be a better option United’s current right-back choices.

“Some fans might question, he’s a right-back, we need a left-back out and out. I’d argue we need a right-back too,” he said.

“I’d argue he’s a potential upgrade on [Noussair] Mazraoui and Diego Dalot and have different styles.

4 Noussair Mazraoui could find his place under threat if United were to go all-in for Spence Credit: Getty



“Mazraoui is a very good footballer with his feet, with his understanding of the game, positionally.

“Going forward, less so but he’s a steady footballer and a very good squad guy to have.

“But, I’d have Djed Spence all day.”

Sports.title: Why Everton are the clear winners in Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil swap deal
Sports.content:
Why Everton are the clear winners in Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil swap deal

Everton have pulled off daylight robbery with a straight swap deal involving Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson.

The two clubs announced on Tuesday morning that McNeil is heading to Selhurst Park, with Johnson making the move to Hill Dickinson - without Everton having to fork out a single penny.



4 Johnson's time at Palace was short lived Credit: Getty

On paper, it is a move that does not immediately make sense, especially considering Palace made Johnson their club-record £35million signing just six months ago.

The 25-year-old has struggled badly since moving to south London, failing to score in 26 appearances for the Eagles.

However, both financially and statistically, Everton are getting the far better end of the bargain.



Speaking on talkSPORT on Monday, Ben Jacobs explained the situation: "It appears quite damaging for Crystal Palace’s books, but it’s a good old-fashioned swap deal.

"It’s probably the first time it’s happened between two Premier League clubs where there doesn’t appear to be any cash changing hands.



"I agree it’s a surprise, because Brennan Johnson, prior to Strand Larson arriving, was briefly Crystal Palace’s record signing.

"Whereas McNeil has a lower market valuation. He thought he was going in January, only to find there was a last-minute paperwork issue which disappointed him at the time.



"But he was sold on that move, personal terms agreed on a four-year contract. They have now been given permission to start their medicals this morning. This will be one going one way, one going the other in a straight swap deal.

"It does feel like, on paper and financially, the deal to gain Johnson is the better one. But I think Palace would argue that Johnson hasn’t worked out there, and the club has always wanted McNeil."

Everton would never have possessed the financial muscle to purchase Johnson in a standalone transaction had they simply pocketed the £20m Palace originally offered for McNeil in January.

4 McNeil saw a deadline day transfer to Crystal Palace from Everton fall through at the 11th hour in January Credit: Getty



Instead, Everton have made Palace effectively take a £15m hit under the Premier League's new squad cost ratio rules.

Both players must be valued at the same figure for the exchange, and when McNeil's proposed move to Selhurst Park fell through in February, he was valued at £20m.

If this is a true swap deal, and the two players are both valued at £20m, it will represent a £15m loss for Palace.

Will Johnson prove a success for Everton?

His tenure at Selhurst Park was undeniably underwhelming, drawing heavy criticism toward the 25-year-old.



On talkSPORT, Gabby Agbonlahor questioned the deal: "When I saw it, I was like 'I get it'. Certain managers and certain players suit one another. Maybe David Moyes is looking at it an wants more pace in the side, wanting to use him in that way.

"Also, with Dwight McNeil, there was talk he was leaving in January, and the new [Palace] manager has clearly seen enough of him already and wants to bring him in."

4 Johnson scored the only goal in the 2025 Europa League final to win the trophy for Spurs Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Jamie O'Hara replied: "Brennan Johnson has been a myth for a few seasons. He didn’t do it at Spurs. In one of our seasons he got top scorer, but he hides in big games."



Agbonlahor pointed out: "You look at both of them and their output last season - 16 Premier League appearances for Spurs, two goals, zero assists. Then at Palace, zero goals and one assist.

"But then Dwight McNeil last season: 22 appearances in the Premier League, zero goals, one assist, so he’s not doing enough either."

O'Hara replied: "It’s like ‘We’ll give you crap, you give us crap back. Call it quits, no charge’.

"I like McNeil. If I were to pick which player would I rather have, I’d take Dwight McNeil. He’s going to work hard, with a lovely left foot. He gives you something.



"Brennan Johnson is just so frustrating because he’s got all the attributes."

He added: "Maybe it’s a confidence thing, maybe David Moyes might be the right manager for him. He’s got the right attributes, he showed it at Nottingham Forest."

Statistics, however, can tell a different story. Despite Johnson enduring a rough 18 months for Tottenham and Palace, he has remained far more clinical in the Premier League than McNeil.

Since Johnson was promoted to the top flight with Nottingham Forest, he has scored 37 goals across all competitions. During that same timeframe, McNeil has netted just 15 times.



Looking at goals-per-minute, Everton's new recruit finds the net once every 253 minutes, whereas Palace's newest winger scores just once every 908 minutes.

There is a clear gap in clinical edge. The Merseyside outfit are replacing a player with a similar assist rate while more than doubling their goal threat upfront.

Additionally, Johnson offers output that comes from a versatile, high-tempo, vertical approach instead of the structured, possession-orientated role McNeil occupied.

4 Everton were just three points off the Champions League places with seven games left last season but then imploded Credit: Getty



While O'Hara argued the ex-Forest player was disappointing for Spurs, the 25-year-old finished as the club's top goalscorer in the 2024/25 campaign with a total of 18 goals.

In comparison, Everton have not had a player hit that mark since Romelu Lukaku in 2016/17.

Even when McNeil was the Toffees' top scorer in 2023, he managed a grand total of just seven goals.

What will Johnson add to Everton?

A primary criticism of Everton in recent seasons is that the squad has severely lacked raw speed, particularly under Sean Dyche and David Moyes.



When the Premier League published sprint data in April and highlighted the fastest recorded sprints since the 2020/21 season.

Johnson featured 15th on the list by clocking 36.70 km/h against Manchester City in 2023.

With Spurs' Micky van de Ven and Wolves' Jackson Tchatchoua each appearing twice on that list, statistically only 11 Premier League players have achieved a higher top speed than the 25-year-old.

Moyes can now harness Johnson's explosive pace in counter-attacking setups—a vital asset for an Everton side that registered the fourth-lowest possession average in England's top flight last term.

Sports.title: Scotland told to make U-turn on hiring 51-cap player to get Champions League winning manager
Sports.content:
Scotland told to make U-turn on hiring 51-cap player to get Champions League winning manager

Scotland have been urged to ditch plans to appoint Steven Naismith as their new boss in favour of Rafael Benitez.

Former Scotland international Naismith is the frontrunner to replace Steve Clarke as boss with a decision expected before next month’s Nations League fixtures.



3 Naismith (centre) was part of the Scotland coaching staff for the World Cup qualifiers and the tournament itself Credit: Getty

Naismith was part of Clarke’s backroom team and is being primed for the top job despite having an ill-fated spell as Hearts boss on his managerial roll of honour.

Scotland told to hire Benitez instead

Scottish FA (SFA) chiefs have a huge decision to make on the direction of their next head coach and former midfielder Gary McAllister believes they should cast their net further in the search for a new boss.

Ex-Portugal manager Roberto Martinez and Everton boss David Moyes have also been linked with the vacant role.



However, McAllister, who clocked up 57 caps for his country, believes former Liverpool and Newcastle boss Benitez is the standout name among the current available options.

“With Roberto Martinez and Moyesy, I don’t think they’re gettable,” McAllister told talkSPORT. “The salaries they’ve been working for, I don’t know if the SFA pay that.



“Rafa’s looking for a way back in.”

And it appears that the 61-year-old has been doing some digging of his own on Benitez.

“All the guys I’ve played with in my little, short period at Liverpool and the players that played under Rafa speak so highly of him,” McAllister added.



“The discipline, the preparation. He’s a winner as well, he’s won everything.

“Somebody like that is who you’d want as an international manager. He’s been there, seen it and done it and has got vast amounts of experience.”

3 Rafa Benitez is looking for a way back into football after his sacking as Panathinaikos boss Credit: Getty

The Spaniard has been out of work since being dismissed by Greek giant Panathinakos in May after only managing a fourth-placed finish in the play-offs of the Greek Super League.



McAllister’s recommendation would mean the SFA pulling the plug on Naismith, who already has experience of the national team set-up.

But the ex-Leeds and Liverpool midfielder believes there are no standout names in the running for the job.

“I know it might never happen but there’s no outstanding candidate for me, I don’t see one," McAllister added.

“Steven Naismith, Clarkey’s assistant might just be a step too much for his first job.



"I think Derek McInnes would have been in contention if he hadn’t gone to Glasgow Rangers.”

3 Gary McAllister says he has reservations over the possible appointment of Naismith Credit: talkSPORT

Naismith's record

Naismith’s time in the Hearts dugout saw him pick up a 43.1 per cent win rate.

He was handed the reins on an interim basis following the dismissal of Robbie Neilson before being handed the job full-time in June 2023.



Prior to his spell with the Hearts first team, Naismith worked with the club’s academy to build up his coaching expertise.

He subsequently went on to become the club’s development manager.

Sports.title: Borussia Dortmund scout behind Jude Bellingham and Erling Haaland wanted by Premier League clubs
Sports.content:
Borussia Dortmund scout behind Jude Bellingham and Erling Haaland wanted by Premier League clubs

Newcastle United and Tottenham Hotspur are interested in Borussia Dortmund scout Sebastian Krug, talkSPORT understands.

Krug, who is seen as playing a key role in Dortmund signing Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham, is wanted by a other European clubs.

4 Haaland and Bellingham proved to be two of Dortmund's best ever signings Credit: Getty

The 43-year-old was appointed as Dortmund's chief scout in 2022 and has worked exclusively with the German giants.

Other names that he has scouted and played roles in signing include Jadon Sancho and Jamie Gittens as well.

More recently, he managed to prise Jobe Bellingham away from Sunderland ahead of numerous Premier League sides to continue the Bellingham affiliation with Dortmund.

He identified both of the Bellingham brothers early on and focused on establishing a good connection with the family.

As a result, he is thought to be someone they trust, and this along with several other high-profile purchases has made him of interest.

Newcastle and Spurs are looking to revamp their recruitment models, and the feeling with Krug is he's reached the end of his time of Dortmund after ten years of service.

Krug's buys at Dortmund

In the time that Krug has been at Dortmund, the club have made some seriously impressive transfers.

Since becoming chief scout alone, Karim Adeyemi, Nico Schlotterbeck and Julian Ryerson arrived in his first year.

Felix Nmecha and Serhou Guirassy have also come through the door, while huge sales for Jude, Haaland, Gittens and Donyell Malen have gone through.

4 Gittens was another one who Krug extensively researched Credit: Getty

4 Haaland and Bellingham were sold for a combined fee of over £150million Credit: Getty

Newcastle restructure

Eddie Howe has left St James' Park, and Matthias Jaissle is in.

The Magpies have Howe's cousin Andy in a prominent recruitment role, along with sporting director Ross Wilson.

Wilson has overseen the majority of the business this summer, with Newcastle shifting focus away from domestic recruits to young, European talent.

The oldest player they've signed this summer is new goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek from Braga, and he is only 24,

Long-serving chief scout Steve Nickson is also set to leave once the transfer window closes.

He was responsible for scouting and helping sign some of Newcastle's best players in recent years, including Joelinton, Allan Saint-Maximin, Alexander Isak and Sven Botman.

However, he is set to take on a new role as director of football for Wrexham, meaning Newcastle will need a new chief scout.

4 Isak is one of Nickson's recruits, but Newcastle will need a new man to lead that department Credit: AFP

Jaissle's requirement

New Toon boss Jaissle has promised 'adjustments' to the squad between now and the end of the transfer window.

Speaking at his first press conference at St James' Park, the German made it clear that he is positive about more players arriving on Tyneside before the Toon face Liverpool in their opening match on August 23.

He said: "We are totally aware internally which positions we might need to strengthen the squad.

"But this is nothing for here, for the press conference. We believe in the players that we have now. And we had a chat after the match in Valencia where you were really happy that the young lads getting the chance, so that's also the approach from this club.

"Every minute they're getting, then they can grow.

"Like I said in my first statement, there will be adjustments in the squad. We still have time."

Sports.title: Paul Scholes tells Manchester United to hijack transfer for ‘nutter’ Premier League player
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes has urged Manchester United to hijack Atletico Madrid's move for Cristian Romero , despite branding him as an 'idiot'.

Tottenham captain Romero looks set to leave north London this summer, with LaLiga giants Atletico closing in on his signature.

5 Romero's five-year stay at Spurs looks to be coming to an end Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands a fee is close to being agreed to bring the Argentina star to the Spanish capital.

Romero has already agreed personal terms with Atletico, who have stolen a march on Napoli after they previously agreed a £34million deal to sign him.

However, they failed to get player buy-in, leaving the door open for Atletico.

While their proposed fee for Romero is yet to be revealed, it's understood Spurs could make a loss on the £43m they paid Atalanta to sign him in 2021.

Last-minute raid for Romero?

Despite Romero's next destination appearing all but confirmed, Manchester United legend Scholes has urged his old club to make a late play for the centre-back.

The Red Devils are keen to bolster their options this summer, with Champions League football returning to Old Trafford this season.

This means Michael Carrick will need a bigger squad to rotate, and Scholes has surprisingly called for Romero to be a quality addition for United if they are to be competitive.

That's despite the Argentine drawing criticism for his poor disciplinary record, having been sent off twice in 23 league appearances for Tottenham last term as they narrowly avoided relegation.

Discussing potential transfer targets for United on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast: "This is one you might laugh at - Cristian Romero from Tottenham.

“I know he’s a nutter. I know he’s got disciplinary issues.

5 Could Michael Carrick steal Romero from under Atletico's noses? Credit: Getty

5 As well as two red cards last term, one of them against Man United, Romero was also booked ten times in the Premier League Credit: Getty

“But I just think he can be a very good centre-half and I think someone like Michael (Carrick) could really calm him down.

“And you’re talking £30million or £40million. This is a fella who’s played centre half and won the World Cup.

“Now, like I said, I know he’s got issues, disciplinary issues.”

Romero has divided opinion during his Premier League career, with Spurs fans turning on him at the back end of last season.

The 2022 World Cup winner became embroiled in a storm in May when it was reported that he was to miss Tottenham's crucial final game of the campaign in favour of a return to Argentina to watch first club Belgrano, before later having a change of heart.

His conduct has even led talkSPORT's Dean Saunders to label him one of the worst captains in Premier League history, but Scholes believes his fiery streak can be channelled positively.

5 Scholes insisted that Romero could unlock his best form at Old Trafford Credit: YouTube/The Good, The Bad & The Football

He continued: “I actually think he’ll go to Atletico Madrid, but, you know, talk about ‘mavericks’?

“And I know he’s a centre half, but do you know what I mean? He’s got that bit of an idiot about him.

“It’s not a very nice thing to say, you know, a bit like [Eric] Cantona did. Obviously, Cantona was a centre forward. It’s a little bit different, more creative.

"But I just think he could become a bit of a cult hero type.

On his disciplinary record, Scholes added: “Funnily enough, that’s what I like about him. There’s a bit of maverick about a centre-half. Do you know what I mean?”

'Desperate for centre halves'

At first glance, United aren't short of options at centre-back, which includes Harry Maguire, Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt, Ayden Heaven and Romero's Argentina teammate Lisandro Martinez.

5 Romero has formed a formidable centre-back partnership with United's Lisandro Martinez for Argentina Credit: Getty

However, centre-back duo Martinez and Maguire have both been prone to injuries in the past, and Scholes insisted Romero could provide experience alongside United's youthful other options, including the 19-year-old Heaven.

On the Red Devils' defensive picture, he rounded off: “I think they're desperate for centre halves, the centre halves aren’t good enough.

“I actually quite like the young kid - Ayden Heaven.

“He's still making little mistakes. He's young, but I think he could be very good, and I wouldn't mind seeing him with Romero actually.

“Look Martinez - the thing with two centre-halves at Man United, especially in that position, you need to rely on them to be fit all the time. You can't rely on these two.

“Harry's [Maguire] picked up his injuries. Martinez, he gets something all the time, doesn't he?"

Sports.title: John Obi Mikel makes brutal dig at Arsenal fans over Vinicius Jr transfer failure: ‘Don’t know what they were smoking’
Sports.content:
John Obi Mikel makes brutal dig at Arsenal fans over Vinicius Jr transfer failure: ‘Don’t know what they were smoking’

John Obi Mikel has taken aim at Arsenal fans for their reaction to the club's interest in Vinicius Jr.

The Premier League champions saw a move for the Brazil forward fall through last week as he penned a new Real Madrid deal.

4 Vinicius Jr has signed a new deal with Real Madrid following Arsenal's interest Credit: AFP

Vinicius Jr is now contracted at the club until 2032 with his previous deal expiring at the end of the upcoming season.

As a result, Arsenal had weighed up a blockbuster move for the star forward this summer.

They had the capacity to sign him and afford his wages but no formal approach was made and the 26-year-old opted to remain with Real Madrid anyway, much to the frustration of Gunners fans.

Mikel has now poked fun at their excitement over the potential deal after it failed to materialise.

It comes after talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor labelled Arsenal supporters delusional during the transfer saga.

Arsenal 'delusion'

Agbonlahor's stance has now been echoed by Mikel on the latest episode of his The Obi One podcast.

The former Chelsea midfielder said: "I don’t know what the Arsenal fans were expecting.

"You win the league after 22 years and then you all of a sudden think: that’s it, you’ve arrived, you’re one of the big boys again. No, you’re not.

"They’ve just been humbled because I said: ‘there’s no way Vinicius Junior is leaving Real Madrid to go to Arsenal, a club that’s won one title in 22 years.’

"This guy wins titles, he’s won lots of titles at Real Madrid. He wants to win titles season after season, the Champions League, LaLiga, competing year after year and winning those titles.

4 Mikel fired an X-rated dig at Arsenal supporters over their reaction to the Vinicius Jr saga Credit: Getty

"He’s tasted what it feels like winning the Champions League, Arsenal have never won the Champions League. Zero.

"You expect a player who has won the Champions League with Real Madrid to leave that, everything that he’s built at Real Madrid, and the squad that Jose Mourinho is assembling right now?

"They look to me like a team that at the end of the season, you probably see them in the Champions League final.

"There’s some team there at Real Madrid when you look at the players that they have. You expect him to leave that and go to a team that has won one league title in 22 years? F****** hell."

Arsenal ended their 22-year wait for a Premier League title by pipping Manchester City to top spot last term.

Mikel Arteta's side also reached the Champions League final, but were beaten on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain.

4 Mikel has questioned what Arsenal fans were thinking amid their interest in Vinicius Jr Credit: The Obi One Podcast

Whilst the Gunners are yet to be crowned European champions, Vinicius Jr has twice lifted the trophy since joining 15-time winners Real Madrid in 2018.

Mikel's Arsenal fan DMs

Mikel continued: "All the Arsenal fans when I said that before, in my DMs, I saw messages, ‘We’ve clipped this, we’ve sent this video, and when it happens we’re absolutely going to come on here and destroy you…’

"I was looking at it and thinking that’s just my opinion. I never thought he was going to leave. He was using you guys to get a better deal, he was using them to get a better deal.

"I have no idea why Arsenal fans would genuinely believe that Vinicius Junior was going to go from Real Madrid to Arsenal.

"If you ask anybody, I think it was only Arsenal fans who believed that was going to happen. I don’t know what they were smoking."

Despite the setback in their pursuit of Vinicius Jr, it has already been a busy summer for Arsenal.

4 Arsenal have signed midfielder Bruno Guimaraes after missing out on Vinicius Jr Credit: Getty

His compatriot Bruno Guimaraes is the latest player to join the club, completing a £75million move from Newcastle.

Christos Tzolis has also arrived from Club Brugge to replace the departed Leandro Trossard.

Elsewhere, Piero Hincapie's loan from Bayer Leverkusen has been made permanent and Arsenal have also signed goalkeeper Illan Meslier.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest told next Elliot Anderson transfer they can sell for triple in a year
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest told next Elliot Anderson transfer they can sell for triple in a year

Ousmane Diomande could provide Nottingham Forest with a huge future cash windfall.

The Ivory Coast international completed a £34.3million switch to the City Ground on Tuesday in what could be a real coup for the Midlands club.



5 Diomande could be Forest's next jewell in the crown Credit: Getty

The centre-back, who spent four seasons in Portugal with Sporting Lisbon, was Forest boss Oliver Glasner’s defensive priority this summer.

It has been an eventful summer of ins and outs at the club led by Elliot Anderson’s £116m switch to Manchester City.

The England international initially joined the Tricky Trees from Newcastle in a £35m deal in 2024.



Forest’s development of the midfielder saw them recoup a whopping £81million in fees and according to European football expert Andy Brassell, Diomande could earn the club a similar fee in the future.

The 22-year old completes an impressive-looking back three alongside Nikola Milenkovic and Murillo and Brassell believes Anderson’s exit will not weigh too heavily on Glasner’s side.



Brassell told talkSPORT.com: “I don't see it as a massive departure for Forest because it's not that dissimilar a signing really to Milenkovic because of course he was cheaper and he was a little bit older.

“But I remember when Forest signed him (Milenkovic) I was like, ‘whoa, yeah, the Premier League does have real power’, because realistically, I could have seen Milenkovic going to, with all due respect to Forest and their history, a bigger club than Forest.



“And ever since he arrived in the Premier League, I've said time and time again there is no more difficult position to adapt to the Premier League than as a defender; it's hard.

“It's really hard because the game is super fast. It's super physical. The referees let more go.

“Teams are fighting for the right to counter-attack, and it's just like, sort of I don't know, crossing a six-lane highway in Texas as a pedestrian.

5 Forest were the recipients of a cash windfall thanks for Anderson's move to Man City Credit: Isaac Parkin / Manchester City FC



5 Brassell believes Diomande could quickly cement himself as a key player for Forest, much like fellow defender Milenkovic (right) Credit: Getty

“We’ve seen some of the best defenders in Premier League history have really difficult starts to their time in the Premier League. I mean Patrice Evra is the most obvious one, I suppose off the top of my head, but Milenkovic adapted so smoothly.”

Brassell believes Milenkovic’s trodden path could be replicated by the club’s latest arrival after impressing during a successful spell in the Portuguese capital.

Brassell added: “I believe that Diomande can do that because he’s someone who's become a really important player for Sporting over recent years.



“Good signing; came with a reputation, but has been coached into someone who really is the real deal.

“They were always gonna sell him this summer; they couldn't hold on to him, and someone like him who's big, can mix it and is tidy on the ball. I don't know what more we could want really from a defender.

“Now, again, we've seen with Forest, I suppose Elliot Anderson being the obvious example, they develop players into players that they can sell on for an absolute fortune and that can finance future rebuilds.

5 Diomande featured once for his country at this summer's World Cup Credit: Getty



“Now, maybe they're not able to do that with Milenkovic.

“Maybe they do it eventually with Murillo, but I think it's fair to say there were more difficult sells than Elliot Anderson was. I don't think Diomande will be a difficult sell.

“If he comes into Forest and does as well as I expect him to do and he sells, and we've seen defensive players do really well at Forest before, as we said, name-checking those two in recent years.

“If he does as well as I would expect him to do, they could sell him for a few times the amount they've paid for him in a year or two time I think.”

After completing his move to the City Ground, Diomande vowed to give his all for the Forest cause this season.



Diomande said: "I am very happy to be here. It is a historic club, and it motivates me to join such a club.

5 Oliver Glasner is constructing one of the Premier League's meanest defences Credit: Getty

"I believe we can achieve very good things this season and I am looking forward to meeting the players and head coach.

"I will give my best and all I can to help the team. I cannot wait to meet the supporters at the City Ground and together we can have a good season."

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez are married! Portugal star ties the knot with influencer in an 'intimate and private' civil ceremony attended by their five children
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez have married in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal.

The couple tied the knot in an 'intimate and private' ceremony on Tuesday with their five children present, a year after they first got engaged.

Ronaldo shared that he and Georgina had tied the knot after ten years together by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram.

He captioned the post: 'C❤️G.'

A representative for Ronaldo also confirmed news of the union, saying: 'Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez were married today in a civil ceremony in Cascais, Portugal, and are now officially husband and wife.

'The ceremony was a private and intimate moment attended by their five children.'

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez have married in an 'intimate and private' ceremony in Cascais, Portugal attended by their five children

The Portugal star announced that he and Georgina had tied the knot by sharing a snap of their wedding bands on Instagram

The wedding news comes just days after it was thought the couple were set to marry in Funchal Cathedral, leading to thousands of fans gathering outside the church.

However, it was then revealed that the couple were not getting married there at all, and the ceremony turned out to be for an entirely unconnected Portuguese couple from Madeira called Fabio Ramos and Fatima Nicole Cunha Teixeira.

Georgina was working at a Gucci store in Madrid, earning £10 an hour, when she and Ronaldo met in 2016.

Recalling their meeting, Georgina said: 'I was finally able to leave the shop to go home three hours later than I should have and as I was getting ready to leave Cristiano came in with his eldest son and some friends.

'Let's just say it was butterflies in my stomach.'

Cristiano would then pick Georgina up from work in his £1.5million Bugatti – after she had arrived at the shop on the bus.

'Many times he'd come after work', she said in her Netflix series I Am Georgina.

'He would come, I remember once, once in a Bugatti. My coworkers went crazy. They get there on the bus, and I would leave in a Bugatti. I mean people couldn't believe it.'

By December, she quit her job shortly after fans began crowding outside the store.

The following month, the pair made their first public appearance at The Best FIFA Football Awards, confirming speculation that they were a couple.

Cristiano and Georgina made their Instagram debut as a couple in March 2017 when the footballer posted a sweet snap of them cuddling on a couch.

In June of that year, the footballer welcomed twins Mateo and Eva via surrogacy and then five months later, Georgina gave birth to their daughter, Alana Martina.

Then the next month, they announced they were expecting, giving birth to their daughter Alana Martina in November.

The following month, Georgina posed for photos with her newborn daughter Alana for the cover of HOLA!

The pair have two biological children, though she helps raise all five of his kids (Cristiano Jr. (pictured left) hugs his baby sister Eva while Georgina cradles Mateo on her lap, Cristiano (pictured right) holds his two daughters baby Bella and Alana Martina)

Ronaldo proposed to Georgina last year with a huge diamond engagement, having previously said he 'waited' before popping the question

Georgina joked that the soccer star popping the question with an 'enormous' diamond ring was 'the least he could offer' after waiting for so long to propose

Revealing how they came up with the name for their daughter, she said: 'We both chose the name. Cristiano chose Alana and I chose Martina.

'We decided to give her both names that each of us chose. We thought it was even more special.'

In 2022, the couple welcomed twins; however, their baby boy tragically died during childbirth, while his sister, Bella Esmeralda, survived.

Opening up about how he and Georgina coped with the heartache of losing a baby, the footballer told Piers Morgan at the time: 'I feel that we always support each other. Sometimes it's like in a relationship you have good moments, bad moments it is part of the journey.

'But probably in that period, we consolidated it more, the relationship, but even in the worst moments you have to meet, you have to make the thing smooth.

'I learned so many things. I saw the other perspective of the life. My daughter, now which is three years old, she is the queen of the family, who made the house happy.

'Everything happens for a reason. I believe in that. So, we are a blessed family. I am proud of that.'

After nearly a decade together, fans were then desperate to know when Georgina and Cristiano would marry, with their family now complete.

However, in an interview with Marca last year, the Portuguese admitted he hadn't yet married Georgina because he hadn't felt the 'click'.

He said: 'I always tell her, "when we get that click". Like everything with our life, and she knows what I'm talking about.

'It could be in a year or it could be in six months or it could be in a month. I'm 1000 per cent sure that it'll happen.'

In August, the footballer finally popped the question with a giant diamond ring.

Fans speculated the pair got engaged the month before after the model shared pictures of a bridal-themed dinner, complete with 'C heart G' pillows, a six-piece band and stunning white flower arrangements.

She also wore a giant sparkler on her wedding ring finger, hinting at the pair's secret engagement.

Georgina gleefully shared the news on Instagram with a photo of her glitzy engagement ring. 'Yes I do. In this and in all my lives,' she wrote in a heartfelt caption.

Cristiano then revealed that two of his children inspired him to give Georgina a 'not-so romantic' and off-the-cuff proposal.

He revealed that he didn't plan to propose to the 'woman of his life' the night they got engaged, but it felt like the 'right time'.

'It was like 1am. My daughters were in bed sleeping,' the 41-year-old told Piers Morgan in part one of their new interview.

He said: 'One of my friends gave me the ring to offer Gio (Georgina) and as I was giving her the ring, my two kids come in and say 'Daddy, you're going to give the ring to mum and you're going to ask her to get married.'

'I said, "Wow, this is the right moment to say yes." It was the time. I knew that I was going to do it one day but I hadn't planned to do it then.

Cristiano met Georgina in 2016 after he saw her in the Gucci store where she was working

'Because my daughters said that and my friends were filming, it was what I wanted and I offered (the ring). I didn't (get on one knee) because I wasn't prepared but it was a beautiful moment. I made a speech.

'It was simple, I'm not a very romantic guy. Well, I am, but I'm not very romantic, not the kind of guy who brings flowers every week to the home. But I'm romantic in my way. It was beautiful and I knew that it's the woman of my life so I did that and I hope that I did it well.'

Asked about when they plan to tie the knot, the footballer joked: 'Not yet. We plan to do it after the World Cup with the trophy! But she is not the person that likes big parties. She doesn't like it. She likes private things. So I will respect these decisions.

'One thing that I love, she didn't care about the ring. She asked me if I was honest and I said, "I want you and I want to marry you." I didn't cry but I had tears on my eyes.'

Experts estimated that Cristiano splashed out an astonishing £1.5million on Georgina's ring.

Sports.title: Paul Pogba 'set to have Monaco contract ripped up after suffering injury' in latest blow to troubled ex-Man United star
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba's Monaco contract is 'set to be terminated' after the 33-year-old suffered a fresh injury.

The French World Cup winner and former Manchester United star had been trying to revive his career following a doping ban.

But his time at Monaco in Ligue 1 has been disastrous and pre-season this summer was seen by the club as crucial in determining whether he could contribute.

He played 45 minutes in one game before a recurrence of a knee injury last season kept him out of four matches.

And now he has collapsed in severe pain in his leg during a training session, accelerating Monaco's decision to terminate his contract, according to L'Equipe and Nicemartin.com.

Pogba only returned to training last week but sustained the thigh injury in a small-sided game and was scheduled for an MRI this week.

Paul Pogba is set to have his contract at Monaco terminated after suffering an injury

The club will now try and reach an agreement with Pogba and his representatives over paying out his deal, which expires next summer.

Daily Mail Sport understands he was offered to MLS clubs in America on Tuesday.

Pogba - who earned £290,000-per-week in his second spell at Man United - is reportedly earning below £44,000-per-week at Monaco.

Pogba was allowed back into football in March 2025 after his doping ban was reduced on appeal.

He had already left Juventus after having that contract terminated by mutual consent in December 2024.

Monaco was his route back into the game but he only managed to play in six matches last term due to persistent injury problems.

It remains to be seen whether Pogba will try to find a new club or decide the time is right to hang up his boots.

Pogba was emotional when he signed for Monaco last summer, describing his comeback as a second chance after what he called 'a time of darkness'.

The midfielder told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.'

Sports.title: Roy Keane's son-in-law could be heading to Portugal, Nottingham Forest complete £36m move for Ousmane Diomande - and Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Roy Keane's son-in-law could be heading to Portugal, Nottingham Forest complete £36m move for Ousmane Diomande - and Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Roy Keane's son-in-law of Portuguese interest

Benfica are weighing up a move for Southampton centre back Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

The Portuguese side sold Antonio Silva to Bournemouth at the start of the month and Benfica coach Marco Silva is looking to bolster his defensive options.

Harwood-Bellis, 24, started out at Manchester City and has been capped once by England, scoring in a 5-0 win over the Republic of Ireland.

He was also part of the England squad that won the 2023 UEFA European U21 Championship.

Harwood-Bellis made 48 appearances and scored seven goals in all competitions last season.

Roy Keane's son-in-law Taylor Harwood-Bellis is of interest to Benfica in Portugal

Hull move back in for Leeds star Gelhardt

Hull City have stepped back in for Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt after Wrexham made an approach to sign him.

The 24-year-old was on loan at Hull last season and scored 14 goals on their way to promotion.

Wrexham were willing to sign him in a £4.5m deal but the chance to play in the Premier League is understood to have swayed the player's decision.

Palace youngster heads out on loan

Bristol City have signed highly rated Crystal Palace wing-back Rio Cardines on a season-long loan.

Cardines, 20, made his Palace debut in their UEFA Conference League win over Dynamo Kyiv last season and went on to make two further appearances for the Eagles while consistently being around the first-team squad.

From Trinidad and Tobago, Cardines has 11 senior international caps to his name and will now look to add Championship experience to his CV.

Palace see Cardines as part of their long-term plans, although he is only contracted until 2028.

The Robins' announcement video featured Cardines drinking a can of Rio in a Caribbean shop while Duran Duran’s ‘Rio’ played.

BOBBY MANZI

Palace consider ex-Brighton man

Solly March has spent time at the Crystal Palace training ground ahead of a potential free transfer.

Brighton released March at the end of last season, with the 32-year-old having played limited minutes over the last three campaigns due to injury problems.

March made 194 Premier League appearances for Brighton, scoring 14 goals and providing 20 assists. He can play on both wings and at wing-back.

A move for March could provoke hostility from Palace supporters, given the Englishman spent 13 years with rivals Brighton. He has scored twice in 11 appearances against Palace.

BOBBY MANZI

Benfica right-back on Toon radar

Newcastle are exploring a move for Benfica right-back Amar Dedic.

The 23-year-old is valued around £25million and has also had interest from Everton.

Born in Austria, Dedic has over 30 caps for Bosnia and Herzegovina.

He started out at Red Bull Salzburg and also had a spell playing for FC Liefering when Matthias Jaissle, Newcastle's new boss, was coaching there.

City's Alleyne is the toast of Clarets

Manchester City defender Max Alleyne is joining Burnley on a season loan.

The 21-year-old who had a spell on loan at Watford last season is expected to undergo a medical in the next 48 hours and could be in the squad to face West Ham on Sunday.

Palace teen on Portuguese radar

Portuguese top-flight club Alverca - who are owned by Vinicius Jr - are in talks to sign Mofe Jemide on a permanent deal from Crystal Palace.

The imposing centre-back, who signed his first professional contract at Palace in 2023, has represented England at U20 level and had significant loan and permanent interest across Europe.

The 19-year-old trained with Pierre Sage’s first team squad in pre-season and was given minutes during friendlies against Swindon, Bromley, Famalicao and Al Ula.

He has yet to make his competitive senior debut, though, turning out 44 times for Palace’s U21s.

EXCLUSIVE BY BOBBY MANZI

Another loan for Kalvin Phillips

Midfielder Kalvin Phillips has agreed to join Sheffield United from Manchester City on another loan, as Daily Mail Sport reported in June.

Midfielder Kalvin Phillips has agreed to join Sheffield United from Manchester City on another loan

Chris Wilder was keen to re-sign the 30-year-old, who has two years left on his contract, despite a difficult loan spell last season.

Phillips made just three appearances for Sheffield United last term and was sent off on his last appearance for the club in the Steel City derby win over Sheffield Wednesday.

Forest target twins

Nottingham Forest are closing in the signing of former Reading twins Joseph Ntege and Jubilee Ntege.

The twins were born on a Stockholm council estate in Sweden and moved to London with their mother and grandmother. They have already represented the country at U15 and U16 level.

Reading spotted them playing grassroots football and beat off competition from Arsenal, Crystal Palace and Fulham to sign them.

The 16-year-olds have attracted interest from a number of clubs following their departure from Reading this summer with Forest, German side Augsburg, Norwich City and Belgian club Genk all in the mix for their signature.

Left winger Joseph has also attracted attention from Manchester United and Newcastle United.

Last season, Joseph registered 35 goals and assists, including 12 goal involvements for the U18s, while Jubilee registered 33 goals and assists, including 10 goal involvements for the U18s

World Cup star joins Forest

Nottingham Forest have completed the £36million signing of Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon.

The 22-year-old centre-back has signed a four-year deal with an option for another year.

Diomande said: 'It is a historic club, and it motivates me to join such a club. I believe we can achieve very good things this season and I am looking forward to meeting the players and head coach.

'I will give my best and all I can to help the team. I cannot wait to meet the supporters at the City Ground and together we can have a good season.'

Forest still want to add a right-back, midfielder and striker.

Nottingham Forest have completed the £36million signing of Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon

Patterson completes Wrexham medical

Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson has completed a medical ahead of his £8m move to Wrexham.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed yesterday, the 26-year-old has agreed terms on a four-year deal with the Championship club.

Patterson is finalising the paperwork on his contract.

Wrexham are also in talks to sign Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt in a £4.5m deal.

Baggies strengthen midfield

West Bromwich Albion have fended off competition from Swansea City to sign Rabby Nzingoula from Ligue 1 side Strasbourg for an undisclosed fee.

The 20-year-old midfielder has agreed a three-year contract and becomes the club's seventh signing of the summer.

Nzingoula made 15 first-team appearances for Strasbourg, including in the Europa Conference League, and has also had loan spells with Montpellier and Nuremberg.

'From the games I have seen, it's clear to see it's a very good, physical and demanding division,' he told West Brom's website.

Ex-Everton star back on Merseyside

Former Everton midfielder Tom Davies has been back training with the club.

The 28-year-old is a free agent and looking for a new club after leaving Sheffield United and has been welcomed back at Everton's Finch Farm training ground where he has been working with the club's U21s to maintain his fitness.

Hull get their Nobel prize

Hull City have finally agreed their protracted negotiations for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

The centre back is heading over for his medical after the clubs settled on a £21million fee plus 12.5per cent sell-on clause, while his former club Real Betis receive 20 percent as part of their sell-on.

The 21-year-old Senegal international can play at centre back and left-back.

Fulham snap up Southampton's Charles

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons.

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year contract, tying him to Craven Cottage until June 2031, with a club option to extend by a further 12 months. Southampton also retain a 20 percent sell-on.

Speaking to FFCtv, Charles, who will wear the number 19 shirt, said: 'It’s a great club, with a really good vision – the manager explained that to me. To be here is a massive privilege.

'I hope to really kickstart my Premier League career. At such a good club as well, it’s perfect for me, and hopefully perfect for the fans as well.

'I’m buzzing to finally get it over the line. The club has got a really good foundation, from the bottom to the top really.'

Palace and Everton complete rare swap deal

Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil have completed their respective swaps to Everton and Crystal Palace and signed four year contracts.

Johnson, who only joined Palace from Tottenham in January for £35m, told evertontv: ‘I'm so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it's a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.

Brennan Johnson has completed a move to Everton from Crystal Palace in a rare swap deal

As part of the transfer, Dwight McNeil has moved the other way to link up with the Eagles after his transfer to the club on Deadline Day in the winter window collapsed at the last moment

'There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in. You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I'm a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

He becomes the fifth summer signing for David Moyes’ squad after Merlin Rohl’s loan obligation was activated along with the additions of Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Christian Norgaard.

Meanwhile, McNeil has signed his four-year contract with Palace and said: 'The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It’s something that I want to be a part of, so I’m really looking forward to getting started.'

Lukaku agrees Turkey move

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli.

The Belgium international has agreed a two year contract worth around £8.6m a season and has already passed his medical.

The deal includes further add ons based on performances.

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli

Chelsea are understood to have inserted a 40percent sell-on clause when they sold Lukaku for a knockdown £26m to Napoli two years ago.

He scored 14 goals in his first season but injury and the arrival of Rasmus Hojlund from Manchester United restricted him to just seven games last year.

Liverpool starlet wanted in Portugal

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move.

The 18-year-old who has joined the club from Austria Vienna in a £2.5million deal has stood out for the first team in pre-season friendlies.

But despite the promise he has shown, and Liverpool's dearth of defensive cover, post-Brexit rules mean Austria youth international Ndukwe doesn't have enough points to obtain a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE) to obtain a work visa.

He will start against Como in their last friendly but is unable to play a competitive match for the Anfield club.

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move

Now clubs from Germany, Spain, Denmark and France have been calling to take the 6ft 6ins centre back on loan but there is a sense Portugal may be his preferred destination.

After playing alongside him, captain Virgil van Dijk said: 'Big talent, big guy and he wants to learn. I had a brief conversation with him, especially in the last couple of days. For him, it is just progressing. I know he has to go on loan I think so let's see where he ends up.'

Napoli still in the hunt for Badiashile

Napoli have offered a £2m loan fee for Chelsea's £30million-rated centre-back Benoit Badiashile with obligation to buy.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs and the player's representatives to try and find a full agreement.

Chelsea have sold Trevoh Chalobah to Como and are also looking to sell Axel Disasi who has had interest from Crystal Palace and West Ham.

Napoli are continuing talks to sign Chelsea's £30m-rated centre-back Beniot Badiashile (right)

Mamadou Sarr, who suffered an injury at the weekend, is likely to go on loan to a Premier League side.

Keeper Filip Jorgensen has completed his move to Strasbourg on loan.

Wigan Athletic are closing in on their loan move for Chelsea midfielder Reggie Walsh while Portsmouth want 17-year-old Chelsea winger Ryan Kavuma-McQueen on loan.

Napoli remain keen on Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus also as talks continue. Arsenal want £20m for the Brazilian.

Villa defender wanted in Belgium

Aston Villa right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic is a target for Rangers along with Hugo Siquet of Bruges.

Nedeljkovic has had interest from a number of clubs including Osasuna but Rangers are exploring a £4million deal with initial loan for the Serbia international.

The 20-year-old had a spell with RB Leipzig last season.

Burnley after new keeper

Burnley are showing interest in OH Leuven goalkeeper Tobe Leysen.

The 24-year-old former Belgium U21 international has one year left on contract so Leuven are willing to listen to offers.

Sports.title: Inter Milan step up pursuit of Spurs star Djed Spence as Italian giants offer £25m for England defender
Sports.content:
Inter Milan are continuing their pursuit of Tottenham full back Djed Spence.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, the Italian side first made contact in June and are trying to work out a compromise fee for the England international.

Inter are offering £25million, only £5m more than the original package given to Middlesbrough when Tottenham signed Spence back in 2022. Spurs were originally looking for closer to £36m.

Spence, who started four games for England at the World Cup, including the semi-final against Argentina, has fallen further down the pecking order at Spurs after the arrival of Andy Robertson from Liverpool.

He signed a new four-year contract in north London at the start of last season but is believed to be keen on joining the Italian champions, with Destiny Udogie and Pedro Porro expected to be Roberto De Zerbi’s preferred full backs this season.

One big plus for Spence though is he is able to play on either side, with many of his Spurs and England minutes coming at left back despite naturally being right-sided.

Inter Milan are willing to pay £25million to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham this summer

He could yet stay in north London but would not be first choice and may be keen for more minutes after his stock rose at the World Cup.

Tottenham, meanwhile, could be as keen to cash in when his value is potentially at its highest.

Sports.title: Awkward moment footballer is blanked by his girlfriend dubbed 'Uruguay's Kim Kardashian' after swooping in for a kiss at his transfer unveiling... before hilariously trying to style it out
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A footballer hoping for a smooch on one of the proudest days of his career was left with lonely lips after his girlfriend blanked and abandoned him on stage.

Uruguay striker Luciano Rodriguez was celebrating his loan move to Brazilian giants Cruzeiro alongside his girlfriend Anto Ciavaglia.

But just as he leaned in for a kiss in front of the cameras, Ciavaglia – who has been dubbed the 'Uruguayan Kim Kardashian' – turned and left him stone cold.

Rodriguez's smile vanished and he was forced to awkwardly stand on his own for a few seconds before running his hand through his hair.

Footage of the awkward moment has gone viral on social media, and Ciavaglia has had to quell any talk of a rift between them.

The 23-year-old model, who has more than 170,000 Instagram followers, said: 'When I entered, I greeted him and when I left, I was very nervous.

Uruguay striker Luciano Rodriguez was blanked and abaondoned by his girlfriend as he went searching for a kiss upon joining Cruzeiro

The forward, 23, tired to style out the awkward moment by running his hand through his hair

His girlfriend, Anto Ciavaglia, who has been dubbed the 'Uruguayan Kim Kardashian,' said she had simply been nervous and did not mean to disrespect him

'The moment overwhelmed me and I preferred to give him space.

'There was no disrespect or anything like what they are trying to make it seem like.'

One clip has been seen more than 4.6 million times.

In more footage from the unveiling, Rodriguez's mother was seen breaking down in tears as she sat next to Ciavaglia, no doubt proud of her son.

Rodriguez, 23, has plenty to celebrate in his career. The striker has been capped five times for his country but narrowly missed out on a place in Uruguay's World Cup squad.

He has also won the Under-20s World Cup and the Uruguayan Premier Division when he was at Liverpool Montevideo in 2023.

After two seasons in Brazil with Bahia, he switched to Neom in the Saudi Pro League last campaign but only scored six goals in 30 games. He has now linked up with Cruzeiro on loan with a reported £14.95million buy option.

At Cruzeiro, he links up with former Leeds forward Luis Sinisterra and ex-West Brom man Matheus Pereira.

His girlfriend, Anto Ciavaglia, was reported by Uruguayan newspaper El Pais to have been dubbed the 'Uruguayan Kim Kardashian' in 2021.

Commenting on the comparison, she told the outlet: 'It's super cute because I love her. I'm a huge fan.'

Sports.title: Arne Slot reveals why he withdrew from Netherlands job talks less than THREE MONTHS after being sacked by Liverpool
Sports.content:
Former Liverpool manager Arne Slot has revealed he turned down the chance to manage the Netherlands because he wants to remain in club football.

The Premier League-winning manager was in negotiations to take over the national team of his homeland after being sacked as Liverpool boss in the summer, but withdrew from the race.

Ronald Koeman had departed following the World Cup, and Slot was the favoured replacement by many as he found himself out of work.

Some reports suggested Slot had turned down the opportunity because of potential salary and contract length, but the 47-year-old has released a statement revealing the true reason.

'Over the past few weeks, and particularly the past few days, various reports have appeared regarding the vacancy at the Dutch national team, suggesting that I had withdrawn from the process after lengthy negotiations, including regarding salary and contract duration,' Slot said via Dutch publication Voetbal International. 'That speculation is incorrect. We simply never reached that stage of the talks.

'At this stage of my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day. Something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team. And why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like.'

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (left) has revealed why he turned down the opportunity to manage the Netherlands

'It would be a great honor to represent my country as national coach one day. However, this was not the right moment for me.'

Slot was sacked by Liverpool at the end of May, just one year after the Dutchman had led the Reds to the Premier League title.

His dismissal came after Liverpool finished fifth in the Premier League at the end of a campaign where Slot oversaw 20 defeats in all competitions.

Slot also came under pressure from supporters and saw several key players – such as the now-departed Mohamed Salah – speak out about the playing style.

He was sacked following a review into Liverpool’s troubled season that was led by Richard Hughes and Michael Edwards, chief executive of football at the club’s owner, Fenway Sports Group.

Prior to joining Liverpool, Slot had led Feyenoord to the Eredivisie title and the Dutch Cup, while they also finished as runners-up in the Conference League.

He was linked with a move to Al-Ahli in Saudi Arabia after Newcastle appointed Matthias Jaissle, but turned down that opportunity too.

Sports.title: How Ronald Araujo jumped at the chance to join Liverpool - and why 'humble' and 'old school' defender solves three problems for Andoni Iraola, reveals LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
If Liverpool fans have had one gripe this summer, it is that their long search for a Mohamed Salah replacement has dragged on and on, with drawn-out sagas for first Yan Diomande and now Bradley Barcola.

But as for the two players they have signed, it's been as easy as uno, dos, tres. Spanish World Cup winner Victor Munoz arrived for £34.5million from Osasuna in June, and yesterday it was the turn of Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo.

It is understood the Reds only made contact with the Uruguay international’s camp last Wednesday. From that point on, Araujo only had one thing on his mind: make this move happen.

Araujo spoke to new Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola and was immediately sold on the move, a view furthered by talks with sporting director Richard Hughes. This was an opportunity he could not pass up – he has always wanted to play in the Premier League.

He wanted the move so much, in fact, that he took a pay cut to make it happen. While Liverpool will cover his salary in full, Araujo will not receive as much as he did at Barcelona.

If the season-long loan goes well, the Reds have agreed a £47.1million fee to make it permanent.

Ronald Araujo's loan move from Barcelona will help to ease Liverpool's defensive crisis

The versatile Araujo can cover at both centre-half and full back and will likely be thrown straight in by Andoni Iraola

There have been reservations among some fans about Araujo's ability and reliability but the positives of this move far outweigh the negatives.

First, his arrival alleviates a gaping hole in Liverpool’s back line – one that Iraola had identified as a problem area given a multitude of defensive injuries.

Just eight minutes into the first pre-season friendly, Joe Gomez limped off with a muscle injury and he will not be available for the beginning of the Premier League season.

Young duo Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni also remain sidelined, while Virgil van Dijk is 35 and only contracted to the end of the coming season. Losing Ibrahima Konate, the experienced French defender who joined Real Madrid for nothing, was a major blow.

Jacquet is set to resume full training this week, it is understood, while Leoni is in the final stage of rehabilitation after missing the best part of a year with a ligament problem. Jacquet has also not played since February so, even if the pair were fit, they will need a bedding-in period.

Araujo, who has played 213 times for Barcelona and won LaLiga on three occasions, can help the duo settle slowly rather than be thrown in at the deep end.

The other big positive about Araujo's arrival is that he can fill in at right back, another problem area given Conor Bradley’s long-term injury.

Need cover for Jacquet or Leoni? Step up, Araujo. Need cover for Bradley or Jeremie Frimpong? Step up, Araujo.

Experts in Spain say Araujo is an old-school defender who likes to get stuck in

Araujo (pictured with wife Abigail and his daughters Aitana and Adara) is a family man whose favourite pastime is spending time with his loved ones

Sources say the 27-year-old is not the most vocal of players in the dressing room but he has a strong presence and gains the respect of team-mates. Instead of hiding when times get tough, he is said to be keen to get involved and step up.

He remains humble and has always stayed in touch with friends from back home in Uruguay. A fan of firing up his barbecue on days off, Araujo is a family man whose favourite pastime is spending time with his loved ones.

With those LaLiga titles under his belt, to go with two Copa del Rey winner's medals, Araujo knows what it takes to win. He has also featured twice in the team of the season in Spain.

But his journey to this point has not always been straightforward. The glare of life at Barcelona has caused Araujo issues with anxiety at points. Several poor performances led to his family receiving death threats. He took a break from football in late 2025.

In an interview with The Athletic before the World Cup, he revealed: ‘I’m going to tell you something that might come as a surprise. Even though I haven’t played that many minutes, this has been the season I’ve learnt the most.

‘I’ve grown a lot mentally. I’ve learnt to be a better husband, a better father, to see things differently, to put things into perspective. People think that because we’re footballers and earn a lot of money, we don’t have any worries, but we do.

‘A lot of things happen in the world of football, and they build up, causing you stress. You can play on a Wednesday and be the best in the world, while on Saturday you lose and you’re the worst.’

Araujo should be lauded for taking his mental health seriously and stepping away to work on his wellbeing. So too for speaking out so frankly. For the Barcelona captain to do that must be inspiring to other players struggling around the world.

The defender has struggled under the scrutiny of life at Barcelona during recent seasons

He has had troubles on the pitch, too, and his form has been inconsistent at times. He has missed 40 games over the last two seasons through absences, physical or mental, according to Transfermarkt. The defender has also been shown four red cards in his career.

Despite the caveats, Liverpool believe Araujo brings important qualities with his experience, leadership and versatility. A source in Spain told Daily Mail Sport this was ‘100 per cent a top signing’ and discussed Araujo's old-school defensive traits, such as a desire to get stuck in.

He is extremely competitive and enjoys taking responsibility in duels. He is quick, strong in the air and old-fashioned in the sense that he loves the physical side of the game. He has developed his on-the-ball game, too.

Another reason to be cheerful for the Reds is they have ticked off a priority position on their shopping list without spending a fee. It allows them to focus on signing at least one forward.

Araujo’s name was a surprise in a summer where many centre backs have been churned out by the rumour-mill. Tottenham’s Micky van de Ven was strongly linked, while Ezri Konsa of Aston Villa was also said to be one considered.

There was talk of Chelsea’s Josh Acheampong and Maxence Lacroix, then of Crystal Palace, while Club Bruges' Joel Ordonez was a name that never went away after January links.

But that talk is over and it is Araujo who has emerged as solution to Liverpool's defensive crisis.

Sports.title: Liverpool get 'multiple calls' over taking star who Andoni Iraola is banned from playing
Sports.content:
Liverpool get 'multiple calls' over taking star who Andoni Iraola is banned from playing

The Liverpool young centre-back has enjoyed an impressive Liverpool pre-season so far before leaving out on loan for the new season

View 2 Images Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe is not short of suitors (Image: (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images))

Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe is not short of suitors and he reportedly already favour a move to Portugal. The 18‑year‑old, who joined from Austria Vienna in a £2.5million deal, is expected to be loaned out for the upcoming season.

‌



Ndukwe impressed for the first team during pre‑season friendlies, but must now head out on loan due to work‑permit complications. Liverpool require a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE) from the FA to secure a work visa from the Home Office, yet the defender does not currently qualify, with players needing 15 points across several criteria.

‌



Having made just one senior appearance for Austria Vienna last season and being signed largely on the back of his standout performances at the Under‑17 World Cup in Qatar, he has not yet accumulated enough points to meet the senior international threshold.

‌



Liverpool sign Ronald Araujo as club legend reaches out and Andoni Iraola gets his wish READ MORE :

At the time, his agent Georg Lederer confirmed the plan had changed after the defender failed to qualify for a visa.

"The fact is that in the 2025/26 Premier League season, clubs had two exception spots where they didn't have to reach this points target," he explained to ORF, as quoted by Sky Sports Austria. "In the new season, this extra rule will be reduced by one spot. A loan club will now be found where Ifeanyi can gain playing experience at a very high level."

According to The Mail, clubs in Portugal, Germany, Spain, Denmark and France have all enquired about taking Ndukwe on loan, but there is a growing sense that Portugal may be his preferred destination.

‌



"I can't say which clubs we are in dialogue with, but I can confirm that we are in dialogue with Danish clubs about Ifeanyi Ndukwe," Lederer added. "The only thing I can say is that we are not talking about the top clubs in Denmark.

View 2 Images Liverpool youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe in action during pre-season (Image: (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images))

"We are also talking to several foreign clubs, but right now we need to decide, in collaboration with Liverpool, where Ifeanyi will fit best. We are looking at several different parameters. First and foremost, it is about Ifeanyi getting a lot of playing time, and then Liverpool are also looking at what type of football clubs play, as they want him in a high-pressing defence, so it is a bit like what you see in Liverpool.

‌



"Since Ifeanyi has just arrived at Liverpool, it is of course a loan agreement without an option to buy, but for now I can't say much more."

Liverpool paid around £2.6m for the teenager in January ahead of his planned move this summer, following his 18th birthday in March. Since then, he has caught the eye in defence during pre‑season outings against Sunderland, Wrexham, Leeds United and Monaco.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Virgil van Dijk, who partnered a player 17 years younger than him in Sunday's 3-2 defeat to Monaco, was left impressed by the youngster.

"Obviously I saw the games in pre-season in America," Van Dijk said. "He's a big talent, big guy and he wants to learn and I had a brief conversation with him, especially in the last couple of days. For him it is just progressing.

"I know he has to go on loan I think so let’s see where he ends up. Yeah [it's a shame he has to move on loan].

Article continues below

"I don’t know exactly what the rules are but the matter of fact is that he has to go on loan and wherever he goes, he needs to learn, get better and be ready when he comes back to hopefully stay there."
