World.title: Paramount CEO may remove operations from California over stalled merger
World.content:
Paramount Skydance’s CEO David Ellison warns of a California exit if the US state does not agree to settlement talks, according to media reports.

Paramount CEO David Ellison may pull his operations out of California if the state does not end its attempt to block the company’s merger with Warner Bros Discovery and agree to settlement talks as soon as October.

The rumours were first reported by the publication Variety on Tuesday. They signal Ellison may be willing to leverage economic pressure on California’s ailing film industry in order to push through the merger.

Al Jazeera was not able to independently confirm the validity of the report.

In July, California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced that he was leading a coalition of 12 state attorneys general in an antitrust lawsuit to block the consolidation.

Should Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery combine, Bonta warned that the resulting company would control 27 percent of theatrically released films in the United States and a third of the country’s basic-cable output.

“Consolidation here not only leads to higher prices,” Bonta said. “It also leads to fewer opportunities for important stories to come to life, and fewer ways for audiences to encounter stories, ideas, and perspectives beyond their own experiences.”

But Variety reported that Ellison told Paramount’s senior executives that he would begin the process of moving the company out of California on October 1 if Bonta does not agree to settlement talks.

There could be downstream effects as well. The report also alleged that Ellison would pull Warner Bros Discovery out of California, too, if the $110bn merger goes through.



Variety indicated that Paramount is considering relocating to the US states of Tennessee, Texas or Georgia — none of which are involved in the ongoing antitrust lawsuit.

A growing enterprise

The dispute over Warner Bros Discovery’s fate stretches back to late 2025, when the company’s sale was first announced.

Critics quickly observed that the sale had the potential to shift the balance of power in Hollywood, with Warner Bros Discovery wielding influential properties including the news channel CNN, the production company New Line Cinema and the television-streaming service HBO.

The streaming giant Netflix initially emerged as a frontrunner to take over Warner Bros Discovery, but by February, Paramount succeeded in inking an agreement.

It was the second major merger Paramount had lined up in less than a year. In 2025, it had also succeeded in consolidating with the media production company Skydance, in a deal that generated scrutiny about the editorial independence of its subsidiaries.

Paramount’s decisions that year to cancel The Late Show with Stephen Colbert and enter into a $16m settlement with US President Donald Trump were widely perceived as efforts to curry government favour for the merger.

Paramount is considered a titan in US filmmaking and media production, as one of the oldest studios in the country. Its portfolio includes CBS News and Paramount Pictures.

A pair of lawsuits

The impending merger with Warner Bros Discovery has led to a fresh round of scrutiny for Ellison and the Paramount leadership.

Last week, Ellison addressed some of those concerns in an opinion column in The New York Times.

In it, he questioned whether the states’ antitrust lawsuit was “really about market share”, speculating that it was instead about control over major news outlets like CNN. He also sought to portray himself as politically independent.

“I have regularly voted for candidates of both parties; I hold some views that would be called conservative and others that would be called liberal, just like most Americans,” Ellison wrote.

“When it comes to our news operations, I do not aspire to lead these companies to bend their newsrooms to my views.”

But the states have argued that combining Warner Bros Discovery and Paramount would create a monopoly, stifling competition.

If the merger succeeds, the states say that only four distributors would control 86 percent of the country’s films.

The merger could also mean job losses. As of the end of 2025, the headcount at Paramount stood at 17,600, while Warner Bros Discovery had 35,500 employees.



A day after the 12 states filed their lawsuit, the Writers Guild of America (WGA) followed suit.

In its July 14 complaint, the guild argued that the merger would mean fewer jobs and more pressure on writers to accept less favourable working terms, owing to reduced competition in the media market.

“Writers will be paid less and have fewer employment opportunities,” the WGA complaint said.

In Los Angeles County alone, the merger could result in a loss of nearly 2,500 jobs, according to an analysis by the Los Angeles County Department of Economic Opportunity, published in June.

As many as 6,000 employees around the world could also see their positions cut.

By comparison, when the Paramount and Skydance merger was completed in 2025, the company laid off roughly 2,000 people.

Costly standoff

On July 24, Paramount Skydance agreed to pause the merger until a ruling in the states’ case is ultimately made or until June 1, 2027 — a move the WGA celebrated.

“It remains our view that this merger is unlawful, and we will continue the fight to block it,” WGA said at the time.

The WGA did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

Slowing the merger could be costly for Paramount Skydance. Under the terms of the merger, the company would have to pay a so-called ticking fee of $7m per day, or $650m per quarter, if the deal does not close by September 30.

But the standoff with Ellison could also be costly for California, which is experiencing a downturn in the number of productions filmed in the state. New York, another state involved in the lawsuit, could see a backlash, as it houses studios for CBS News and Paramount’s executive offices.

Representatives for the state of California and Paramount Skydance did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

Paramount Skydance’s stock is trending upward on the heels of Tuesday’s report. The stock was up 0.4 percent in midday trading, while Warner Bros Discovery was up 1.1 percent.

World.title: Rescuers scramble for survivors with 180 dead in Colombia earthquake
World.content:
Rescue workers in Colombia are working against the clock to free survivors trapped in buildings and under rubble following Monday's powerful earthquake.

More than 180 people have been confirmed dead - most in the cities of Cali and Pereira.

The magnitude 7.4 quake struck at 07:34 (12:34 GMT) on Monday and was felt across an enormous area, stretching for hundreds of miles across western Colombia - with fresh aftershocks still being felt on Tuesday.

While the official death toll remains 181, an aggregated figure gathered from local officials puts it higher - potentially at more than 240. A state of emergency has been declared by President Abelardo de la Espriella.

Giving an update on Tuesday from Pereira, one of the worst hit cities, President Espriella said as well as those killed, almost 2,600 had been injured, and almost 200 people remain missing.

He also reported that more than 1,100 homes had been destroyed, and more than 8,000 had been damaged.

Overnight on Monday into Tuesday, several people several people spent the night outdoors in cities like Pereira and Cali - either due to their homes being destroyed, or fear of further collapses.

Across the country, dozens of larger buildings have also collapsed.

World.title: Trump hid in catering truck in secret plane swap over Iran threat, reports say
World.content:
Donald Trump secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month, as part of an elaborate ruse in response to a possible Iranian threat, US media report.

The US president boarded Air Force One in view of television cameras before being transported to a military aircraft with the help of a catering truck, the Washington Post said. Journalists and some White House staff on board did not know he had been smuggled out.

Officials told the BBC's US partner CBS News that the US had detected a credible Iranian threat to fire a missile at the plane. The White House has not confirmed the secret switch.

Trump had earlier said he was Iran's "number one target" during the summit in Ankara.

The clandestine manoeuvre came a day after the US renewed military strikes on Iran following a breakdown of negotiations between Washington and Tehran to end the war.

Trump had arrived in Turkey aboard a newer Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar, but announced that he would leave on the old Air Force One "for old time's sake".

On 8 July, footage showed him boarding the presidential jet at Ankara airport. But according to the Washington Post, he was then secretly taken to a smaller C-32A military aircraft - a modified Boeing 757 often used by the vice-president - via a catering truck which had been elevated to plane level on the opposite side to where he had boarded.

World.title: Russia using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine, Zelensky says
World.content:
Ukraine and Russia have continued striking each other overnight, with President Volodymyr Zelensky accusing Moscow of using North Korean missiles.

Ukraine said strikes on the southern city of Zaporizhzhia - which killed seven people and injured at least 24 - involved ballistic missiles from Russia's ally.

In Voronezh, western Russia, warehouses of the biggest online retailer Wildberries were hit by Ukraine. The company, known as Russia's Amazon, has been repeatedly targeted in recent weeks.

The attacks come a day after at least 13 people were killed, including one child, in Ukrainian drone strikes on the Russian republic of Tatarstan, more than 1,100 km (680 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

In a video address on Monday evening, Zelensky said "for the first time" Russia "cannot wage war without reinforcements from North Korea".

"The more North Korean strikes there are here in Ukraine, in Europe, the more their missiles and soldiers are used, the more they correct their shortcomings and blind spots", Zelensky said, adding that this poses a danger to the rest of the world.

He has not presented any evidence to back up his comments.

It is not the first time Zelensky as well as other senior Ukrainian and Western officials have accused Russia of receiving military assistance from North Korea.

Ukraine's military has said that says dozens of North Korean missiles have been fired by Russia into its territory since Moscow's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

The Ukrainian president warned over the weekend that as many as 50,000 North Korean soldiers were being sent to fight with Russian forces.

Some 11,000 North Korean soldiers were deployed to help Moscow push Ukrainian troops out of the western Russian region of Kursk following their cross-border incursion in August 2024.

In January 2025, Western officials told the BBC that North Korean troops had suffered nearly 40% casualties in the fighting there in just three months.

In his Monday's address, Zelensky also hailed a successful air strike on a Russian petrochemical plant in western Siberia on Monday as a "very significant achievement" by the Ukrainian military.

He promised "more Ukrainian deep strikes, which should demonstrate to Russia and the Russians that peace is necessary".

Zaporizhzhia regional head Ivan Fedorov posted photos of vehicles and buildings on fire, saying Moscow had struck the city using missiles and guided bombs.

All seven casualties were employees of Ukraine's Zaporizhstal metallurgical plant, which later halted all its operations.

One person was injured in strikes on the capital Kyiv, where air raid sirens sounded twice during the night. Explosions could be heard on the outskirts of the capital, triggering fires.

Local officials later said a children's hospital was damaged - but there were no injuries as staff and patients were sheltering.

Two women have been injured in a Russian drone strike on the north-eastern Ukrainian city of Sumy, according to regional head Serhii Kryvosheienko.

He later said that one person was killed when Russia attacked the city with gliding bombs in the afternoon.

Meanwhile, strikes on substations in Kherson and Kharkiv resulted in power outages.

Ukrainian officials say Russia fired 120 drones overnight and a range of different missiles, but for the first time they have not given a number of missiles fired or intercepted.

It follows an Air Force statement on Monday urging the media not to write "sensationalised headlines" or "spread pessimism" about the shortage of air defence interceptors.

Separately, there have been reports of a fire and explosions at a logistics centre of Wildberries in the Voronezh region.

Wildberries has not yet confirmed the attack, but said that its facilities in the region, which borders Ukraine, have been evacuated.

In July, Ukrainian drone attacks on several retail warehouses belonging to Wildberries disrupted the operations of a large number of small and medium-sized Russian businesses.

Kyiv said at the time it was targeting logistics hubs used by Russians to buy military equipment, and disrupting supplies to the Russian army.

The attack on Tatarstan this week was one of the deadliest single attacks on Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

At least 75 people were injured in the strikes, with Ukraine's Armed Forces saying it had hit the city's Tanevo oil refinery.

Verified images on social media showed large plumes of smoke and flames rising into the sky in daytime, with air raid sirens howling in the background.

The Uzbek consulate in Tatarstan said seven of those killed were citizens of Uzbekistan.

World.title: Russia releases former US Marine reported in poor health
World.content:
President Donald Trump said a US Marine held in a Russian prison, whose health was reportedly in extremely poor condition, has been released.

"After my discussions with President Vladimir Putin, Russia has agreed to release him, very much on a Humanitarian Basis," Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that no prisoner swap took place.

In 2022, Gilman, who is from Massachusetts, was arrested for allegedly kicking a police officer while aboard a train. He had recently been moved from prison to a civilian hospital in Russia after going into a catatonic-like state.

Trump said the 32-year-old was on a flight back to the US accompanied by his mother, doctors, and members of the administration.

According to a statement from his family, Gilman is expected to later arrive at a US military hospital in Texas where he will be assessed and treated.

His health was in "life-threatening condition" after he was subjected to "harsh and abusive treatment", the family said.

"The Russians treated my brother so badly. They hurt him for no reason, other than that he was both and American and a Marine," his sister, Lexi Hudson, said in the statement.

"I am so grateful to President Trump for saving my brother's life," she added.

Massachusetts Senator Ed Markey also helped secure her brother's release, she said.

In a statement, Markey said: "Approximately 50 days ago, Robert was diagnosed with a dissociative stupor - a condition where he is non-responsive and unable to interact or eat. "

In Russian confinement, Gilman was subject to repeated harassment, including forced exercise training sessions that lasted up to 16 hours and the administration of psychotropic drugs, Eric Lebson, who advocated for Gilman's release as part of the group Global Reach, told CBS News, the BBC's media partner.

The abuse was so severe that at one point Gilman had required a feeding tube in his nose, according to Lebson.

Gilman served in the US Marines from August 2019 to August 2020.

He was arrested for allegedly kicking a police officer while drunk aboard a train to Moscow in January 2022 and was initially given a sentence of three and a half years.

He was later found guilty of assaulting prison guards, after he allegedly attacked a prison inspector during a cell check. His sentence was then increased to 10 years.

Lebson said five other Americans remain in Russia, each contending with medical issues. Their names are Aleksandr Antonov, David Barnes, Olga Jezler, Andre Khachatoorian, and Chuck Zimmerman.

World.title: Lebanon parliament votes to abolish death penalty
World.content:
Lebanon's parliament has voted to abolish the death penalty, a move that would make it the first country in the Middle East to formally end capital punishment.

A majority of MPs in the 128-seat parliament backed the measure on Tuesday, while Hezbollah's parliamentary bloc voted against it.

The legislation will now go to the cabinet before being passed to President Joseph Aoun for signing. The government has already expressed its support for the measure.

Lebanon has not carried out an execution since January 2004, although courts have continued to hand down death sentences. Rights groups estimate that more than 78 people remain on death row.

Under the new legislation, capital punishment will be replaced with life imprisonment with hard labour. However, the legislation does not yet set out in detail how the new sentence would be enforced.

Hard labour is already written into Lebanese law but has rarely been implemented in recent years. The country's financial crisis and overcrowded prisons have limited the authorities' resources and capacity.

The latest legislation follows years of campaigning by civil society groups and lawyers for the removal of capital punishment from Lebanese law.

"We cannot solve a crime with a crime or end violence with violence," Oragit Younan told the BBC.

As co-founder of the Lebanese Association for Civil Rights, she led a nearly three-decade campaign to abolish the death penalty in Lebanon.

"We are in a war, and people [have been] killed every day, so even in this situation, we can fight, we can struggle for human rights, and we can win. We can be a model for others," she said.

Tuesday's vote in parliament follows more than two decades of a de facto moratorium on executions. An execution required a decree signed by the president, prime minister and justice minister - but no such decree has been signed since 2004.

Under Lebanese law, the death penalty could previously be imposed for some of the country's most serious offences, including aggravated murder, certain terrorism-related crimes resulting in death, treason, espionage and offences against state security.

Previous attempts to abolish the death penalty have failed, including legislation introduced in parliament in 2004 and a proposal from the justice ministry in 2008.

Lebanon's move comes as the use of the death penalty remains contested elsewhere in the Middle East.

Jordan resumed executions in June, carrying out its first since 2017.

In Israel, its parliament has approved legislation that allows for the expansion of the circumstances in which capital punishment can be imposed.

Israeli MPs passed a new law in May to impose the death penalty and conduct public trials for those involved in the Hamas-led attacks and mass hostage-taking in Israel in October 2023.

Elsewhere, the UN human rights chief has said he is alarmed by the rise in executions in Iran, with capital punishment continuing to be used "to instil fear among the population and suppress dissent".

In Iran, at least 56 people had been executed on national security-related charges since 19 March, including 27 in cases linked to January's nationwide anti-government protests, UN human rights chief Volker TÃ¼rk said earlier this month.

World.title: Ousted Syrian dictator Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia
World.content:
A Syrian court has sentenced ousted dictator Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia, after convicting him of committing war crimes and crimes against humanity during the country's civil war.

It is the first conviction against Assad, who fled from Damascus to the Russian capital, Moscow, with his family after his regime was overthrown in December 2024, ending his family's five-decade grip on power.

Assad's cousin and the former head of political security in southern Syria's Deraa province, Atef Najib, was also sentenced to death. He appeared wearing a striped prison uniform inside a cage in the courtroom as the judge read out his sentence.

Deraa is widely seen as the birthplace of the uprising against Assad's rule.

In March 2011, the detention and alleged torture of a group of teenagers accused of writing anti-government graffiti sparked protests in the city, which were met with a violent crackdown by security forces.

That response helped ignite nationwide demonstrations that escalated into civil war in which hundreds of thousands of people were killed.

Syria's interim government began trying officials associated with the Assad regime, which ruled the country for more than 50 years, earlier this year.

Najib is one of the highest-ranking officials to be put on trial.

He was convicted of crimes including murder, "the intentional killing of children under 15" and "torture leading to death".

The court also sentenced six former military and security officials in absentia to death, including Bashar al-Assad's younger brother, Maher. He ran the army's elite Fourth Division and also fled to Moscow when the regime fell.

The others convicted include former defence minister Fahd al-Freij.

World.title: France bans unsolicited telemarketing calls
World.content:
France has banned unsolicited telemarketing phone calls, in what a consumer group is hailing as a "small revolution" for the sales industry.

From Tuesday, unsolicited calls are prohibited for businesses in all sectors - but there are some exceptions.

Calls will only be permitted if they relate to a contract a person has already entered into or the company has obtained prior consent to be contacted for marketing.

"It cannot be stressed enough that peace and quiet is a right, and it is time to stop exposing consumers to unwanted solicitations," consumer advocacy group Que Choisir Ensemble, said in a statement.

"This observation also holds true online and on the street, which are saturated with demands to consume," group president Marie-Amandine StÃ©venin added.

She said the group had long been advocating "for an end to the automatic assumption that someone in their home or private life is a potential customer."

"This is a victory for consumers, the vast majority of whom do not want to receive sales calls," she said.

But the law change has riled some business groups, and officials in Morocco, where the call centre sector is heavily reliant on the French market.

One government minister estimated the telemarketing restrictions could lead to the loss of up to 50,000 jobs, according to a report in Moroccan newspaper Le Matin.

The head of France's direct-selling trade association, the FÃ©dÃ©ration de la Vente Directe (FVD), also criticised the reforms for adding what he said were administrative burdens for businesses.

"You'll have to obtain written consent from your customer, and you'll also have to keep proof of that consent," FrÃ©dÃ©ric Billon said in comments reported by the New York Times.

According to a 2025 parliamentary report, 97% of people are annoyed by telemarketing calls, with the authors wryly noting it is "one of those rare issues that unites people in France".

The same report found 72% of French people reported being contacted on their mobile phones at least once a week, while 38% said they were called once a day.

Germany, Austria and Italy are among the European countries that impose significant restrictions on telemarketing calls, often referred to as cold calls.

In the UK, most telemarketing calls are legal provided the recipient has not objected to the call and their number is not on a statutory list of people or businesses who do not want to receive calls.

World.title: Former judge removed by Orbán elected Hungarian president
World.content:
Hungary's parliament has elected AndrÃ¡s Baka, 73, a respected judge and former head of the Supreme Court, as head of state.

The Hungarian president is a largely figurehead role, but Baka's rule promises to be tempestuous.

His task will be to monitor Prime Minister PÃ©ter Magyar's efforts to dismantle the interlocking economic and political powerhouse established by former Prime Minister Viktor OrbÃ¡n. He will also oversee the writing of a new constitution, to replace OrbÃ¡n's constitution of 2011.

"We cannot build the new Hungary on revenge," AndrÃ¡s Baka told Parliament, after he was elected by 140 votes to 6.

"The majority of society now feels a sense of liberation and hope. Others feel disappointment and uncertainty," he said. "In a democratic society, this is not an anomaly, but a natural state of affairs."

All 51 MPs belonging to OrbÃ¡n's party Fidesz walked out of the chamber before the vote, in protest against the ousting of their favourite, TamÃ¡s Sulyok, from the post last month.

In his speech, AndrÃ¡s Baka promised the broadest possible debate on the creation of a new constitution.

Since taking office in early May, the new Magyar government has lost no time attacking OrbÃ¡n's legacy.

Twenty-seven laws have been passed, and two amendments to the constitution.

The states of emergency - migrants, Covid, and war in Ukraine - which OrbÃ¡n used to govern by decree, were all cancelled.

The Sovereignty Protection Office, which the Fidesz government used to attack critical journalists and NGOs, was abolished, and an National Asset Recovery and Protection Office was established, with sweeping powers to investigate and prosecute individuals accused of stealing state funds under the former government.

Fidesz accuses the Tisza government of establishing a "tyranny". Ironically, they removed Baka from his post as president of the Supreme Court in 2011, for attempting to stop them undermine the rule of law.

Public service radio and TV have been off air since 9 July, as news programmes are revamped. The stated aim is to restore their independence, from their Fidesz-era role as government propaganda organs.

Other key changes came under Amendments 16 and 17 of the constitution, limiting the prime minister to two terms in office, and MPs to three. The ability of the Constitutional Court to oversee acts of parliament, taken away by Fidesz, was also restored.

If the Tisza majority expects Baka to be a tame president, they may get a rude awakening.

In a BBC interview before he was asked to take the post, he made clear he opposes the limitation of MPs' terms as an intrusion on the right of voters to freely choose their representatives.

Baka served for 17 years as the Hungarian judge at the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg.

"I am not a political man," he told the BBC last month. "I got involved in politics through my professional, legal way of thinking."

Baka was elected today as a transitional figure.

Under the constitutional amendment which made his presidency possible, the new president will likely only be in place until the new constitution comes into force - or for maximum of five years.

Speaking to parliament on Tuesday, Baka made it clear that he intended to push back against the Hungarian tendency to trust in powerful leaders.

"The state is not there for itself," he said, at the end of his speech. "It is there for the people."

World.title: Jos bishop disowns ex-employee implicated in alleged plot to kidnap his wife, another
World.content:
A former worker of the Anglican Diocese of Jos and two security operatives (names withheld) are helping the police over an alleged plot to kidnap the wives of the incumbent and immediate-past bishops, the diocese has revealed in a statement.

The diocese announced that security agencies had intervened before the suspects executed the plot.

It rejected reports portraying the principal suspect as a serving clergyman under the current Bishop of Jos, Ephraim Gongden.

The church said the suspect worked with the diocese but had been dismissed in 2022 by the former bishop and had never been reinstated by Mr Gongden.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The clarification was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the Registrar of the Anglican Diocese of Jos, Harrison Ugwuala.

The statement followed the circulation of reports and photographs on social media, which, according to the church, linked the suspect to the current diocesan administration and portrayed Mr Gongden as being connected to the alleged crime.

Suspect no longer with the Anglican Diocese

According to the diocese, the principal suspect presents himself as a clergyman and had previously worked within the diocese.

“He was NOT reinstated by the present Bishop of the Anglican Diocese of Jos,” the statement said.

“The individual is NOT a clergyman in the employment, authority, or jurisdiction of the Anglican Diocese of Jos,” it said.

“The Anglican Diocese of Jos has no working relationship whatsoever with this individual.”

Reports of the alleged kidnapping plot had identified the suspect as a clergyman, creating the impression that he was still affiliated with the Anglican Church.

The diocese said that the description was inaccurate and could wrongly associate the current church leadership with the alleged criminal activity.

Two bishops’ wives allegedly targeted

The alleged plot involved the wives of both bishops.

The diocese did not disclose how the alleged plot was uncovered or how the suspects were arrested.

It confirmed the kidnap attempt and commended the security agencies for their intervention.

The diocese also did not comment on the alleged roles of the two security operatives or disclose whether they were serving members of any particular security agency.

The matter is expected to be clarified as investigations by the security agencies progress.

Complaint over alleged cyber-bullying

The diocese said it had reported what it described as misinformation and cyber-bullying arising from the incident to relevant security and legal authorities.

It urged members of the church and the wider public to remain calm while investigations continue.

“Evil will not have the last word,” the church said.

The police have yet to disclose the names of the suspects.

World.title: CIBN urges banks to deploy fresh capital to MSMEs as Nigeria targets $1 trillion economy
World.content:
The Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) has called on Nigerian banks to deploy their recently raised capital towards financing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), saying increased lending to the sector is critical to achieving stronger economic growth and Nigeria’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy.

The President and Chairman of the Council of the CIBN, Dele Alabi, made the call at the world press conference on the institute’s 19th Annual Banking and Finance Conference, scheduled for 8-9 September at the Congress Hall, Transcorp Hilton, Abuja.

The conference, themed “Building a Resilient Economy in an Era of Disruptions: Strategic Imperatives for the Banking and Financial Services Industry,” will bring together policymakers, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, technology innovators, academics and business leaders to deliberate on the future of the banking and financial services industry.

$1 trillion economy

Speaking during the question-and-answer session, Mr Alabi said the recent recapitalisation of banks had provided stronger buffers for their balance sheets. Still, he argued that the additional capital should now be deployed towards productive sectors of the economy rather than remaining concentrated in government securities and large corporate borrowers.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Capitalisation provides a buffer for shocks. It insulates banks’ balance sheets, but it does not stop there,” he said.

According to him, the banking landscape has changed significantly, particularly as declining interest rates and tighter borrowing margins among top-tier companies reduce the attractiveness of the traditional approach to deploying bank funds.

“Smart bankers, smart bank CEOs have to think of a more ingenious way of utilising this capital. Capital is not cheap. Capital is the most expensive source of funds. It’s more expensive than debt. Equity capital is more expensive than debt capital,” Mr Alabi said.

The CIBN president said banks should therefore look further down the economic ladder by increasing financing to MSMEs, which he described as critical drivers of economic growth, particularly in emerging markets.

Mr Alabi said the shift would also advance the CIBN’s impact vision, under which inclusion is one of the Institute’s key priorities.

He explained that financial inclusion should go beyond access to basic financial services and ensure that critical participants in the economy, particularly small businesses, have access to finance.

“MSMEs represent the critical growth source for the engine of the growth of the economy. Not only in Nigeria, globally for emerging markets, but MSMEs are also the ones that drive the economy,” he said.

He argued that increased SME financing would provide benefits beyond the banking industry by creating employment, improving business activity and supporting economic development.

The CIBN president also linked the banking industry’s role in supporting productive businesses to Nigeria’s ambition to expand its economy significantly.

He said the financial services sector would remain critical to achieving the government’s long-term economic objectives because of its role in mobilising savings and allocating capital to productive activities.

“It can be widely accepted, and there is empirical evidence to support the fact that an economy cannot grow to a $1 trillion mark without the support of the financial services sector,” Mr Alabi said.

Mr Alabi added that the banking industry was prepared to support the Federal Government in achieving the objective of significantly expanding the Nigerian economy.

“As a group in the financial services industry, we are really ready to support the federal government in achieving this objective of growing the economy of Nigeria significantly in the foreseeable future,” he added.

September Conference

Meanwhile, at the institute’s two-day conference in September, Mr Alabi described it as timely amid technological disruption, geopolitical uncertainties, evolving customer expectations, cybersecurity risks, and climate-related challenges confronting the global economy.

According to Mr Alabi, resilience has become a defining attribute of successful financial systems. At the same time, the conference is expected to provide a platform for policymakers, regulators, financial institutions, and technology innovators to deliberate on issues shaping the future of banking, finance and the broader economy.

He said the conference aligns with the strategic direction of his administration under the Institute’s IMPACT vision, which focuses on Inclusion, Membership Economy, Professionalism and Ethical Conduct, Accountability and Enhanced Financial Performance, Competencies and Skills Development, and Technology, Automation and Innovation.

Through the Conference, we seek to equip industry practitioners with forward-looking insights, strengthen institutional capabilities, and stimulate conversations that will accelerate innovation while reinforcing the professionalism and ethical standards upon which sustainable banking must be built. In doing so, we also advance our broader objective of positioning Nigeria’s banking profession to compete confidently on the global stage,” Mr Alabi said.

The CIBN president said more than 10,000 delegates from Nigeria and across the world are expected to participate in the conference.

He said the expected participants would include banking executives, regulators, government officials, development partners, academics, fintech leaders, investors and other stakeholders in the financial ecosystem.

Also speaking at the briefing, Moruf Oseni, Chairman of the Consultative Committee for the 19th Annual Banking and Finance Conference and Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Wema Bank Plc, who was represented by the Director, Southwest and Specialised Business, Wema Bank, said the conference would provide practical insights and actionable recommendations for strengthening institutions and positioning the Nigerian banking industry for sustained growth.

Mr Oseni said the conference would serve as a knowledge-sharing and solution-driven platform where stakeholders would exchange ideas, share experiences, and develop practical solutions to challenges affecting the financial services sector and the broader economy.

“As customary, the resolutions reached at the Conference will be documented and forwarded to relevant stakeholders and policymakers in the form of a communique, to support informed decision-making, policy formulation, and strategic alignment with global best practices,” Mr Oseni said.

The organisers said President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, and Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, Olayemi Cardoso, are among the dignitaries expected at the event.

According to Mr Oseni, other participants will include leaders from government, regulatory institutions, development organisations and the private sector.

Conference sessions

The conference will feature three business sessions focused on major challenges and opportunities facing the financial services industry.

The first session, titled “Shaping the New Financial System for Nigeria’s Prosperity: The Role of Recapitalisation, AI and Geopolitical Dynamics,” will examine the implications of bank recapitalisation, artificial intelligence and geopolitical developments for Nigeria’s financial system.

The second session, a women-focused engagement, is titled “Inclusive Leadership, Stronger Systems: The Strategic Role of Women in Building Resilient Financial Ecosystems.”

The third session, titled “Navigating Cyber and Systemic Risks in the AI-Driven Future of Banking: Implications for Financial Stability and Business Resilience,” will focus on cybersecurity, systemic risks, financial stability and business resilience in an increasingly AI-driven banking environment.

Mr Oseni said the sessions were designed to address the most pressing issues facing the banking and financial services industry, while exploring strategies to strengthen financial stability, improve cybersecurity and risk management, and accelerate innovation to support sustainable economic growth.

World.title: Osun’s APC senator seen in viral video issuing death threat to Accord Party members
World.content:
Osun East Senator Francis Fadahunsi has issued death threat to members of the Accord Party found in Ilesa ahead of Saturday’s Osun State governorship election.

He made the threat in a viral video that has heightened concerns over escalating political violence in the state.

Mr Fadahunsi spoke in Yoruba while addressing supporters during a protest at the palace of the Owa Obokun of Ijesaland over what he described as incessant killings of the APC members in Ijesaland.

In the video circulating online, the senator, who was accompanied by other All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders accused Accord Party members of killing people.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The cap they wear – it is Yellow Fever cap, it is the cap of an animal,” Mr Fadahunsi said, referring to Accord Party’s yellow brand.

Each of jabs launched at the Accord Party was received an approving cheers from the crowd.

“It is animal that kills. Have you ever heard that APC killed anyone? Are those being killed not your people?” Mr Fadahunsi said.

“So, we have come to tell you, up till the day of the election, if we see them, it is killing.”

The statement came a day after three people were killed in a shooting in the Imo area of Ilesa in Osun State, amid heightened political tension in the community ahead of the 15 August governorship election.

The circumstances surrounding the killings, however, remain disputed.

While sources in the community linked the incident to a clash between supporters of the APC and Accord, the Osun State Police Command said the violence was a cult-related clash involving suspected members of the Aiye and Eiye confraternities.

The police confirm that individuals identified only as Idowu, Yinka and Eja, were reportedly shot dead in the clash, and recorded the recovery of four expended cartridges and two Android phones were recovered from the scene,

Following a distress call, the Commissioner of Police in charge of the election, Samuel Erale Etaifo, ordered the deployment of operatives of the Violence Crime Response Unit (VCRU) to the area.

“The CP Election has directed the VCRU operatives and other tactical teams to intensify patrols, surveillance and intelligence-led operations within llesa and adjoining areas, particularly around identified flashpoints, to forestall any reprisal attack,” the statement read.

The Ilesa’s incident adds to the growing killings, including ones linked to pre-election violence in the state ahead of its 15 August election.

The Nigeria Police Force acknowledged the severity of the situation. In July, the Force disclosed that 30 people had been allegedly killed in pre-election violence incidents in Osun.

“From the complaints received, we cannot rule out the involvement of some politicians in the killings,” said Anietie Iniedu, the Force Public Relations Officer (PRO) during a morning brief programme on Channel TV.

Accord raises alarm over senator’s threat

The Imole Campaign Council, the campaign organisation of Governor Ademola Adeleke, condemned Mr Fadahunsi’s statement and called for his arrest and prosecution.

The council’s Chairman, Media and Publicity, Bamidele Salam, described the senator’s comments as an “open incitement to kill” and said they posed a serious threat to Accord members and other residents in Ijesaland.

The campaign council also alleged that the senator’s statement was consistent with information it had received about the alleged movement of political thugs and fake police officers into Ijesaland.

It further alleged that Mr Fadahunsi threatened to prevent Accord supporters from voting even if they presented their Permanent Voter Cards at polling units on election day.

The council called on the Inspector-General of Police and the Director-General of the Department of State Services to investigate the senator’s remarks and take appropriate action.

“Coming from a serving member of the National Assembly who swore to uphold the constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, we feel compelled to demand that the inspector General of Police and the Director General of the Department of State Security order the arrest of senator Fadahunsi and prosecute him in accordance with relevant laws of the Federation.”

It also urged security agencies to pay particular attention to Ilesa East, Ilesa West, Obokun, Oriade, Atakumosa East and Atakumosa West local government areas during Saturday’s election.

The council said it would hold Mr Fadahunsi responsible for any violence against Accord members in Ijesaland, while urging residents not to be intimidated by the threat.

Senator ‘clarifies’ statement

However, Mr Fadahunsi has issued a “clarification” explaining he did use “kill” in its literal sense.

Tribune reported that the senator’s media office in Osun State issued a statement, titled ‘Kill Osun Accord with Votes, Not Violence, Senator Fadahunsi Tells AP.”

The statement explained that his comment was “a call on supporters to overwhelmingly reject the Accord Party at the ballot box through lawful, peaceful and democratic means during the August 15 governorship election.”

“For the avoidance of doubt, the Senator’s statement was purely political and metaphorical,” the statement added, while maintaining appealing to APC supporters and other political actors to maintain peace and obey the law before, during and after the election.

“At no point did Senator Fadahunsi advocate violence, intimidation or any form of physical attack against members or supporters of the Accord Party or any other political party. His consistent position has always been that elections should be decided by the votes of the people and not by force.”

He also called on security agencies to remain professional and ensure that every eligible voter is able to exercise their constitutional right without fear or intimidation.

“Senator Fadahunsi remains committed to democratic values, issue-based campaigns and a credible electoral process. He believes that the will of the people, freely expressed through the ballot, must always prevail.

“We, therefore, appeal to members of the public not to misinterpret or deliberately distort the Senator’s comments, as they were clearly intended to encourage electoral victory through the power of the ballot and not through violence,” he stated.

Rising tension ahead of Saturday’s poll

The latest controversy comes amid a surge in politically linked violence across Osun in the final days before the governorship election.

The state has recorded shootings, killings, attacks on political supporters and other violent incidents during the campaign period, prompting increased deployment of security personnel and calls for political parties to restrain their supporters.

The police have repeatedly warned political actors and their supporters against acts capable of disrupting the election.

With voters expected to go to the polls on Saturday to choose among 14 governorship candidates, including Mr Adeleke who is seeking re-election, concerns over violence have intensified in several parts of the state.

World.title: Abiodun to Ogun Monarchs: Mobilise subjects for peaceful, responsible 2027 polls
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has charged traditional rulers across the state to deploy their influence at the grassroots to mobilise their subjects for peaceful, responsible and informed participation in the 2027 general elections.

Mr Abiodun made the call on Tuesday while inaugurating the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo, as the new Chairman of the Ogun State Council of Obas at the Obas’ Complex, Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta.

The governor urged the monarchs to educate their subjects on the importance of civic participation and encourage them to shun violence, thuggery, hatred and other acts capable of threatening the peace and stability of the state before, during and after the elections.

He described the 2027 elections as an important democratic transition, stressing that the strength of democracy was measured not only by the votes cast but also by the peace, responsibility and sound judgment with which citizens exercised their franchise.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, traditional institutions, given their reach and moral authority at the grassroots, have an important role to play in ensuring that the next electoral season does not undermine the peace and development recorded in the state.

He said: “Beyond security, I also called on our royal fathers to continue mobilising our people towards responsible civic participation, particularly as we enter another electoral season.

“Our people should be encouraged to recognise and support the development strides of the government and, when the time comes, translate their appreciation into their democratic choices at the polls.

“At the same time, you must remind your subjects that elections should never become an excuse for violence, hatred or division. We must continue to uphold the peace we have collectively nurtured and participate responsibly in programmes that advance our ‘Building Our Future Together’ agenda.”

Mr Abiodun said his administration had, over the past seven years, strengthened mechanisms to discourage hooliganism and political thuggery, noting that the recent primary election conducted by the ruling party in the state was peaceful and crisis-free.

He commended the traditional rulers for their continued support for the administration, describing them as strategic partners in maintaining peace, strengthening security and deepening grassroots development.

The governor particularly praised the monarchs for supporting security agencies through intelligence gathering and community mobilisation, noting that their knowledge of local communities remained indispensable to effective security operations.

He said government could provide technology and logistics, while security agencies could deploy personnel, but neither could substitute for the local intelligence and community knowledge available through traditional institutions and citizens.

Mr Abiodun said the partnership had yielded positive results, particularly in the state’s recent security challenges.

He disclosed that security agencies had arrested all suspects linked to the recent abduction of students of Gateway ICT Polytechnic, Saapade, assuring residents that the government would continue to deny criminals any safe haven in the state.

He said: “I particularly commend you for the assistance extended to our security agencies during our recent security challenges. Information obtained through our communities and grassroots structures has enhanced security operations and demonstrated what can be achieved when government, traditional institutions, citizens and security agencies work together.

“I am therefore very pleased to inform our royal fathers that our security personnel have now arrested all the suspects linked to the recent abduction of students of the Gateway ICT Polytechnic, Saapade.

“Our message is very clear: there will be no sanctuary for kidnappers, criminals, cultists or their collaborators anywhere in Ogun State.”

The governor also urged the traditional rulers to make their palaces centres of peace and conflict resolution by deploying their wisdom and moral authority to settle minor disputes before they escalate into wider community crises.

He noted that effective intervention by traditional rulers at the early stages of disputes could prevent avoidable conflicts and preserve peaceful coexistence within communities.

Mr Abiodun explained that the distribution of 60 Sports Utility Vehicles to members of the State Council of Obas was part of the administration’s efforts to improve the mobility of traditional rulers and enable them to perform their responsibilities more effectively.

He charged the new Chairman of the Council, Oba Gbadebo, to build on the achievements of his predecessor by strengthening unity among traditional rulers and promoting initiatives that would contribute to the advancement of the state.

The Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Ganiyu Hamzat, commended the traditional rulers for their contributions to peace, community development and the preservation of Ogun’s cultural heritage.

Mr Hamzat described the monarchs as custodians of the state’s customs, traditions and cultural values, noting that their wisdom and leadership had continued to promote peaceful coexistence and strengthen the relationship between government and the people.

He urged the traditional rulers to continue to give due consideration to the resolutions and recommendations of the Council in the overall interest of the state.

The commissioner also commended Governor Abiodun for strengthening the partnership between government and the traditional institution, describing the collaboration as strategic to peace, grassroots development and good governance.

He urged the monarchs to reciprocate the gesture by sustaining their support for government programmes and policies aimed at advancing the socio-economic development of Ogun.

Alake pledges to build on predecessor’s legacy

In his remarks, the new Chairman of the State Council of Obas, Oba Gbadebo, commended Governor Abiodun for what he described as the administration’s developmental strides across the state.

The Alake said the administration’s interventions in infrastructure and other sectors had contributed significantly to Ogun’s continued emergence as a major industrial hub in Nigeria.

He also commended his predecessor, the Olu of Ilaro and Paramount Ruler of Yewaland, Oba Kehinde Olugbenle, for his contributions to the welfare, unity and cohesion of traditional rulers during his two-year tenure.

Oba Gbadebo pledged to build on those achievements by fostering greater unity within the Council and supporting government programmes and policies that would improve the welfare and prosperity of the people.

The two-year tenure of Oba Olugbenle as Chairman of the Ogun State Council of Obas ended recently.

World.title: Tinubu approves framework to unlock $50bn deep offshore investment
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved a new investment framework designed to unlock up to $50 billion in deep offshore oil and gas investments and revive major projects that have remained stalled for decades.

The framework replaces project-by-project negotiations with transparent eligibility criteria and a rules-based investment architecture intended to provide greater certainty for investors and improve Nigeria’s competitiveness in attracting global capital.

According to a statement issued on Tuesday by Bayo Onanuga, the president’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, the reform is expected to support the next generation of deep offshore developments, beginning with the approximately $10 billion Bonga Southwest project.

The statement said the decision followed Mr Tinubu’s engagement with Wael Sawan, the chief executive officer of Shell, during which the president directed the development of measures to unlock the next wave of investments in Nigeria’s deep offshore sector.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Rather than pursuing individual solutions for specific projects, the government subsequently developed a broader investment framework applicable to multiple categories of qualifying deep offshore developments.

The framework is being implemented through the Deep Offshore Oil and Gas Projects Incentives (Tax Remission) Order, 2026, according to the statement.

It said the new arrangement would provide investors with clearer eligibility requirements and implementation procedures while safeguarding Nigeria’s long-term economic interests.

The approval also allows NNPC Limited, as the government’s nominated counterparty under the Production Sharing Contracts (PSCs), to proceed with amendments to eligible PSCs required to implement the framework.

Focus on local content

The reform is also expected to strengthen local participation in deep offshore projects by encouraging project execution within Nigeria where commercially and technically feasible.

Olu Arowolo-Verheijen, Mr Tinubu’s special adviser on oil and gas, said the framework would help expand domestic industrial capacity alongside increased investment and oil production.

“Projects qualifying under the framework will maximise execution within Nigeria wherever commercially and technically feasible, strengthening domestic engineering, fabrication, marine logistics, technical services and project management,” she said.

“The objective is not only to increase investment and production, but also to create skilled jobs, deepen local supply chains and position Nigeria as Africa’s regional hub for deep offshore project execution.”

The presidency said the framework was developed through an extensive inter-agency process involving fiscal, legal, commercial and regulatory institutions, as well as industry operators.

Institutions involved include the Federal Ministry of Justice, Federal Ministry of Finance, Federal Ministry of Petroleum Resources, Nigeria Revenue Service, NNPC Limited, Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) and Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board.

Mr Tinubu commended the institutions, investing partners and other stakeholders involved in developing the framework.

‘Certainty will attract investment’

Mr Tinubu said countries that attract long-term investment are not necessarily those with the largest natural resource endowments but those capable of providing certainty for investors.

“The countries that attract long-term investment are not necessarily those with the greatest natural resources. They are the ones that provide the greatest certainty,” the president said.

“This reform reflects our determination to build an investment environment defined by clear rules, strong institutions and enduring partnerships.”

READ ALSO: Tinubu seeks global cooperation to tackle emerging security threats

He added that the government was creating conditions for increased capital inflows, growth of Nigerian businesses and greater national value from the country’s natural resources.

Nigeria has sought to revive investment in its deep offshore oil and gas sector amid concerns over the high cost and complexity of offshore developments and the competitiveness of its fiscal regime.

The Bonga Southwest project, operated by Shell, is one of the major developments expected to benefit from the new framework.

The presidency said the broader reform was designed not merely to facilitate a single project but to establish a durable investment architecture capable of supporting multiple deep offshore developments and attracting substantial new capital into Nigeria’s oil and gas industry.

World.title: Former petroleum minister chief Dan Etete says Abacha didn’t die during sex
World.content:
Former Minister of Petroleum Resources, Dan Etete, has questioned claims that former military Head of State, Sani Abacha, died during a sexual encounter, describing the account as unsupported by evidence.

Mr Etete, who served in the Abacha regime and said he was a close friend of the late military ruler, was reacting to claims by a former State Security Service (SSS) officer, Dennis Amachree, about Mr Abacha’s final hours.

Mr Amachree made the claims in his memoir, DSS @40: My Journey Behind the Shield, excerpts of which were published in July.

He said Mr Abacha suffered a coitus-induced cardiac arrest at about 4:05 a.m. on 8 June 1998 at the Presidential Villa in Abuja.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

But Mr Etete, in a statement titled, “Twenty-Eight Years On, Still No Evidence,” said Mr Amachree had provided nothing to substantiate the account.

He questioned the identity of the woman, her nationality and whether she had ever confirmed the story attributed to her.

He also asked for the post-mortem report and any medical findings establishing how Abacha died.

Mr Etete questioned the alleged interrogation of the woman, asking where the record was, who conducted it and whether it was signed.

He also asked whether flight records, hotel registers or duty logs existed to support the timeline given by Mr Amachree.

“He tells us the time to the minute. He tells us the room. He tells us what was said. Twenty-eight years on, from memory, with nothing on paper behind any of it,” Mr Etete stated.

According to him, the account was never raised during the years following Mr Abacha’s death, when various inquiries and discussions were held about the circumstances surrounding it.

“In twenty-eight years, through every inquiry and every commission, through all the years when the people close to that night were still alive and still talking, this account was never once raised,” he noted.

Mr Etete also questioned why the woman was allowed to leave Nigeria if she was considered relevant to the circumstances surrounding Mr Abacha’s death.

Mr Etete stated that he was not speaking as Mr Abacha’s lawyer or spokesman but as someone who served in his government and knew him personally.

“I do not pretend the record of those years is beyond argument. It is not, and it will be argued over long after all of us are gone. But a man’s death is not entertainment, and a country’s history is not built on the unsupported memory of one man.

“I cannot tell you what is in Mr Amachree’s mind. I can tell you what is in his hands: nothing. No post-mortem. No file. No signature. No woman.

“He did not provide any evidence because they do not exist. Now, for clarity, please address the following as well: What are the so-called woman’s name and her nationality? Why did you allow her to leave the country without filing a serious criminal investigation against her? Who ordered her release and subsequent departure from Nigeria? Gen. Sani Abacha was not an ordinary man or citizen of Nigeria.

“For such an important case which involves the country’s president, it should not be taken lightly and handled by you alone. Let me be very clear here that you are simply seeking cheap publicity and relevance.

“Until the author provides verified, documented answers to those questions—names, nationality, investigation records, authorisation for release, and supporting documentary evidence—no serious reader should treat this account as anything more than an unsubstantiated narrative.

“The account remains unverified, unsupported, and unconvincing. It should not be trusted. It reads as little more than a salacious attempt to attract attention and sell a book,” he added.

Al-Mustapha disputes Amachree’s account

Mr Etete’s comments came after Mr Abacha’s former Chief Security Officer, Hamza Al-Mustapha, also rejected Mr Amachree’s version of events.

Mr Al-Mustapha, speaking with journalists in Kaduna in July, described the account as false and said it did not reflect what happened at the Presidential Villa.

Mr Amachree was serving as Assistant Director of Operations and Intelligence at the Lagos SSS Command when Mr Abacha died.

Mr Al-Mustapha claimed he had evidence to disprove the account, although he did not make the evidence public.

“The boy was asked by others to write those lies. I have all the CCTV footage of what happened in my custody, so what he said is not true,” he said.

He urged Nigerians to disregard the account.

“Just ignore his lies. It’s bad to say such things about someone who is dead,” he stressed.

What Amachree said

In his memoir, Mr Amachree gave an account of what happened at the Presidential Villa in the early hours of 8 June 1998.

He explained that Mr Abacha’s girlfriend had arrived at Aso Rock with her younger sister, a pharmacist who was in Abuja for a conference.

According to Mr Amachree, the girlfriend later returned to her hotel, leaving her sister with Mr Abacha.

He said the woman realised during the encounter that Mr Abacha had stopped responding. She allegedly checked his pulse and found none.

Mr Amachree stated that she panicked, dressed and asked a soldier on guard duty to arrange transport to her hotel.

By the time security officials were alerted, he noted, she had already left Abuja on an early morning flight to Lagos.

Mr Amachree said he was later directed by SSS headquarters to locate and question her.

He claimed his team found the woman and brought her to his office, where he personally interrogated her.

According to him, she told him: “I did not kill him, he died on top of me.”

Mr Amachree stated that he subsequently contacted the SSS Director in Abuja and the woman was flown back.

He said the account showed that Mr Abacha died from what he described as a coitus-induced cardiac arrest and dismissed theories that the former ruler had been poisoned.

Mr Abacha seized power in a military coup on 17 November 1993 and ruled Nigeria until his death.

The federal government noted at the time that he died after a sudden illness. His death has nevertheless remained the subject of speculation, with different accounts emerging over the years from people who were involved in, or claimed knowledge of, the events surrounding his final hours.

World.title: #OsunDecides2026: Adeleke criticises predecessor Oyinlola for not backing him
World.content:
Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke on Tuesday criticised one his predecessors, Olagunsoye Oyinlola, for withdrawing support from him ahead of Saturday’s governorship election.

Mr Adeleke, who is seeking a second term in office, accused Mr Oyinlola of repeatedly working against his political ambitions.

The governor made the allegation on Tuesday during an Arise TV town hall programme ahead of the August 15 governorship election.

The governor said Mr Oyinlola opposed his political ambition during his bid for the Senate and later at the 2018 and 2022 governorship elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, Mr Oyinlola alleged opposition to his political aspirations was not new, claiming that the former governor did not support him when he contested for the Senate in 2007.

Mr Adeleke also referred to the disputed 2018 governorship election, saying the ex-governor did not support him despite then-President Muhammadu Buhari’s comments on the election.

He further alleged that Mr Oyinlola opposed him during the 2022 governorship election by backing the then Secretary to the Osun State Government, Fatai Akinbade.

“In 2022, he did not support me. He went to go and bring the secretary to the state government, Akinbad,” Mr Adeleke said.

Mr Adeleke’s comments come against the backdrop of Mr Oyinlola’s changing political position ahead of Saturday’s election. The former governor, who had earlier supported Adeleke’s re-election bid, withdrew that backing on Sunday and aligned with the APC governorship candidate, Bola Oyebamiji.

Mr Oyinlola and other PDP stakeholders at the Sunday’s event declared support for Mr Oyebamiji, citing what they described as a lack of inclusiveness in Mr Adeleke’s administration.

While announcing the endorsement, mr Oyinlola, however, said he and the other members of his group had not defected from the PDP, insisting that they remained members of the party but had chosen to support Mr Oyebamiji based on their conviction that Osun required a different direction.

Political influence

Mr Adeleke, however, mocked the former governor’s influence, claiming that his presented candidate secured low votes in the election despite the ex-governor’s support.

He said the former governor subsequently approached him after his victory in the 2022 election seeking reconciliation.

According to Mr Adeleke, he accepted the overture because of his willingness to forgive political opponents.

The governor also claimed that Mr Oyinlola complained to him about not having a car, after which he gave him a new vehicle. However, Mr Adeleke alleged that the former governor subsequently changed his political position again and declined to support him.

“Immediately I won, he came back to me. Say, ‘Oh, don’t let us fight. Don’t let us do this.’ I said, ‘Okay, no problem, because I have a forgiving spirit.’ He complained to me…he doesn’t have a car, and I gave him a new car. He collected a new car, and he defected to another party.”

The governor dismissed the former governor’s current position as politically insignificant, saying it would not affect his chances in Saturday’s election.

“He’s a paperweight. I’m not worried about him. That’s not going to affect anything,” Mr Adeleke said.

The latest exchange comes days before Osun voters go to the poll to elect a governor, with Mr Adeleke seeking another term. The All Progressives Congress candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, is among the major challengers in the 14-party contest.

World.title: Rarara’s attack song normal in politics, Kwankwaso tells Pantami
World.content:
Former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Kwankwaso, has criticised former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Pantami, over a recent song by Dauda Rarara, a prominent political praise singer associated with the All Progressives Congress (APC) and President Bola Tinubu.

Mr Kwankwaso, the presidential running mate in the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), said Mr Pantami should not be surprised by his criticism in the song because, by entering partisan politics, he has exposed himself to the attacks that politicians routinely face.

He spoke in an interview with DCL Hausa on Tuesday.

‘Rarara has attacked me, Shekarau, Ganduje’

Mr Kwankwaso, who has himself been targeted by Rarara’s political songs in the past, described the singer’s attack on Mr Pantami as a form of political retribution.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, Mr Pantami had previously used harsh language against him, but he chose not to respond in kind.

“Rarara has insulted me; he has also insulted Shekarau, Ganduje and many other people here in Kano. Yet, we handled it better because we are politicians,” Mr Kwankwaso said.

He was referring to former Kano governors Ibrahim Shekarau and Abdullahi Ganduje, who, like him, have had political differences with Rarara over the years.

Mr Kwankwaso said the controversy surrounding the song was a consequence of Mr Pantami’s decision to move from religious preaching into active partisan politics.

“That is why we say: once you abandon religious preaching and enter politics, you should not expect politicians to treat you as a religious cleric. What Rarara did to Pantami is only the beginning; it is nothing more than a welcome to politics,” he said.

Kwankwaso recalls past clashes with Pantami

Mr Kwankwaso also recalled an occasion when Mr Pantami allegedly attacked his personality in the presence of his supporters.

“Pantami once hurled all sorts of insults at me in the presence of my supporters. I was the one who asked them to calm down and not react,” he said.

He added that there was another occasion when his supporters attempted to confront Mr Pantami.

“There was even a time when my supporters tried to deal with him in Kano because of the way he attacked my personality,” Mr Kwankwaso said.

He argued that Mr Pantami should now understand that political engagement entails criticism from opponents and other political actors.

Pantami’s move into politics

Mr Pantami, a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and prominent Islamic scholar, is running for governor in Gombe State.

He initially sought the APC ticket but withdrew from the party’s primary in May, alleging violations of the Electoral Act 2026 and irregularities in the process.

He subsequently joined the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and emerged as the candidate of the Nyesom Wike-led faction.

His entry into partisan politics has also revived scrutiny of his past comments about the PDP, particularly his criticism of the party. At the same time, he was an Islamic preacher and later a minister under the APC administration.

Mr Kwankwaso highlighted this apparent political reversal in his criticism of the former minister.

“Pantami used to call the PDP all kinds of names, including ‘Al-Kafira’ (the Infidel party), yet he has now joined the same party and contested under its platform,” he said.

PREMIUM TIMES had earlier reported that Mr Pantami’s political transition and his emergence as a PDP governorship candidate generated debate, particularly over his past criticism of the party.

Rarara’s song sparks controversy

The latest controversy began after Rarara released a song widely interpreted as a political attack on Mr Pantami.

The song attracted criticism from Nigerians, with some questioning the use of music to attack political opponents, while others argued that political figures who enter partisan politics should expect criticism.

The controversy also drew reactions from Islamic scholars and other public commentators, who criticised what they considered the use of abusive or derogatory language against a prominent religious figure.

However, Mr Pantami previously acknowledged that criticism is part of politics. In May, while suspending a social media aide who described his political opponents as “hypocrites”, he said criticism was an important part of political discourse and that, as a politician seeking to lead a diverse society, he understood its value.

Against this backdrop, Mr Kwankwaso’s comments have added to the debate over whether religious leaders who enter partisan politics should continue to be treated primarily as clerics or be subjected to scrutiny and criticism as other politicians.

World.title: Why the Middle East war still convulses the oil market – Report
World.content:
Vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas in southern Iran on August 10, 2026. The US President signalled on August 9 that he was prepared to let economic pressure mount against Iran, apparently backing away from more military strikes after Tehran issued a list of demands for opening the Strait of Hormuz. His remarks came after Iran issued over the weekend a list of conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has remained largely closed since the start of the Middle East war in late February. (Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP) /

After more than five months of conflict, oil markets continue to surge and tumble over the latest developments in the US-Iran clash, including President Donald Trump’s shifting pronouncements.

What is behind the market’s volatility?

– The ‘shock’ of Hormuz –

While the potential vulnerability of the Strait of Hormuz has long been viewed as a risk, oil markets have still been caught off guard by Iran’s ability to largely close the crucial waterway.

“What really shakes the market are surprises… and the Hormuz closure was a shock,” said Jim Burkhard, head of global energy crude oil research at S&P Global.

Brent oil prices surged more than 13 percent in the immediate aftermath of the US-Israeli siege against Iran on February 28. Since that time, prices have been jolted in both directions as the conflict has dragged on.

“Number one, it’s the complete unexpectedness, unfamiliarity with what we are seeing,” Bob McNally, president of the Rapidian Energy Group and a former White House energy advisor to George W. Bush, said of the unprecedented curtailment of the Strait.

“There was this perception that the US would never allow it to happen,” McNally added.

About 20 million barrels per day of crude traverse the Strait, roughly a quarter of global oil demand, making the current supply shock “the biggest disruption in history,” according to McNally.

Subsequent events have jerked prices in both directions. Markets were unnerved by the US move to blockade Iran’s ports, but subsequently buoyed by a June 17 agreement between the United States and Iran to cease hostilities.

– An imminent resolution? –

While the conflict has boosted prices overall, international benchmark Brent oil has averaged $94 a barrel since the start of the fighting, well below the $150-per-barrel level seen by some experts as possible.

One explanation is the market’s response to Trump, who has issued contradictory statements but has often described a Hormuz resolution as within striking distance. Such statements have helped keep crude prices from rising more.

“The market believes and still believes that this crisis can and will end soon,” McNally said.

Optimistic statements by the president and other Trump administration figures like Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have often sent oil prices sharply lower, posing peril to traders on the wrong side.

“The oil market has sort of burned the bulls so many times you just don’t have bulls willing to go in and trade,” McNally said. “So all you have is people who are trading, especially these algorithmic traders who are just trading on headlines.”

The Hormuz closure has lowered volumes by about 12.6 million barrels per day, according to JPMorgan Chase analysts.

Some of this has been blunted by lower crude imports from China, while releases from commercial and government inventories have also offset the effects of lost supply.

In March, the International Energy Agency announced member governments would release 400 million barrels of oil, the largest emergency stock release in history.

The United States, Canada and Brazil have been among the countries increasing output.

Middle East producers have maneuvered some shipments away from the Strait. For example, Saudi Arabia shifted crude exports to the Red Sea, but that avenue has also been compromised by attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels.

– Not just oil –

While the fluctuations of crude prices generate most of the headlines, analysts have also highlighted the stresses on refined products, including gasoline.

“The most pressure in the world today is on refined products because there is generally enough crude oil out there right now, but there’s not enough refining capacity,” Burkhard said.

Diesel prices have doubled compared with February, while gasoline prices are up about 50 percent.

The Middle East conflict has also sidelined key energy infrastructure due to attacks, including some refinery capacity. Energy experts also point to Russian refinery outages due to attacks from Ukraine in that war.

Continued robust demand for petroleum products has led to a historic surge in refinery profit margins, resulting in huge earnings windfalls for large oil companies in the second quarter.
