World.title: Mokambo road works to proceed-DC
World.content:
Mufulira District Commissioner Evaristo Chilumba has assured residents that the $56.7 million Mufulira-Mokambo road project will proceed uninterrupted beyond the upcoming general elections, dismissing claims that the infrastructure initiative is merely a political campaign gimmick.

Speaking during an onsite inspection of the ongoing engineering works, Mr Chilumba emphasised that the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) agreement underpinning the road was established long before the electoral cycle.

He urged members of the public to have faith in President Hakainde Hichilema’s administration, citing its unwavering commitment to delivering critical national infrastructure.

“This project will not stall and it will continue even after the general elections,” Mr Chilumba stated.

He noted that the arrangement was secured independently of political timelines and urged residents to have faith in President Hakainde Hichilema and the government’s commitment to ensuring the road’s completion.

Mr Chilumba pointed out that construction of the road had initially commenced under the Patriotic Front government, stating that money had been spent yet works had not been done.

He explained that when the United Party for National Development government came into power in 2021, they commenced the process of construction from scratch, including having to find a new contractor.

“The contractor is currently on site conducting the road works and the project is moving,” the District Commissioner said.

Mr Chilumba disclosed that graveling works have so far been done on the entire stretch of the road up to the border, while noting that tarring of some patches of the road has already commenced.

He stated that the project is expected to be completed by the end of 2026.

Mr. Chilumba stated that the comprehensive infrastructure upgrade includes upgrading the carriageway from Mufulira to Mokambo to bituminous standard, constructing a modern toll plaza, and building a modern border post at Mokambo.

He said that the modern border post will help in speeding up the clearing process of trucks going to the nearby Democratic Republic of Congo.

Highlighting the immediate local impact, Mr Chilumba noted that for many years, residents using the road were subjected to spending about over an hour travelling from Mufulira to Mokambo due to the bad state of the road.

“After the works are done, residents will now spend less than 30 minutes travelling to the border,” he said.

Mr Chilumba said the road will ease access for residents and improve mobility on the road.

He stated that residents suffered, being stuck in mud and potholes, especially during the rainy season for many years, due to the bad state of the road, adding that this will all be a thing of the past thanks to government’s commitment to ensure that the road is completed quickly.

Mr Chilumba noted that the road is of benefit to the entire country as it connects Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) thereby boosting inter-country trade.

World.title: NW UPND calls for re-election of Hichilema
World.content:
United Party for National Development (UPND) Northwestern Provincial Chairperson Adam Sepezo has called on voters to re-elect President Hakainde Hichilema in the August 13 general elections, to enable the government to continue implementing its development agenda.

Mr Sepezo says the UPND administration has recorded significant progress in various sectors of the economy since assuming office in 2021.

He noted that the achievements include investments in education, health, agriculture, social protection and employment creation.

Mr Sepezo was speaking to the Zambia News and Information Services (ZANIS) in Solwezi district, shortly after a stakeholder meeting with the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) at Solwezi College of Education.

He said President Hichilema had delivered on most of the UPND’s 2021 campaign promises, including restoring peace and order and addressing political violence and cadreism.

Mr Sepezo said the re-election of President Hichilema will provide an opportunity for the government to consolidate the gains made and further transform the economy.

He cited sustainable agriculture, mechanisation, social protection programmes and the Constituency Development Funds (CDF) as some of the interventions that have contributed to improving people’s livelihoods.

Mr Sepezo said education remains a key priority for the government, citing the reintroduction of free education, the school feeding programme, increased meal allowances for students and the recruitment of teachers.

He said the government had also recruited health workers, Zambia Police Service officers, Zambia National Service personnel and members of the Zambia Army, among others.

‘‘The recruitment of workers across various sectors demonstrates the government’s commitment to creating employment opportunities for Zambians,’’ he said.

He has, however, urged citizens to maintain peace and unity before, during and after the elections.

Mr Sepezo further called on political players and their supporters to reject political violence and resolve differences through dialogue and lawful channels.

World.title: President Hichilema describes late Mr Liato, as a dedicated public servant
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has described Former Cabinet Minister in the Movement for Multi-Party Democracy (MMD) administration, Austin Liato, as a dedicated public servant who made a significant contribution to the development of Zambia’s labour sector.

President Hichilema notes that the late Mr Liato, distinguished himself through many years of dedicated service to the country, particularly during his time in the Ministry of Labour and Social Security.

ZANIS reports that President Hichilema made the remarks in a speech read on his behalf by Secretary to the Cabinet, Patrick Kangwa, at a Funeral Church Service held at Anglican Cathedral of the Holy Cross in Lusaka today.

President Hichilema said Mr Liato, working as a Cabinet Minister, provided leadership and oversight to one of the most critical sectors of the economy.

He added that the late minister played an important role in maintaining cordial relations between the Government and the labour movement.

President Hichilema said Mr Liato promoted dialogue and an open-door policy, which helped foster harmony in the labour market and contributed to increased investor confidence, job creation and economic development.

He further described the late Mr Liato as a respected trade unionist who laid a strong foundation for improved labour relations between Government, trade unions and other stakeholders.

In his Eulogy, Oasis of Blessings Assembly Bishop, Max Nalumango, said Mr Liato was a man of determination, a family man and cherished his friends, adding that he admired his sense of humor.

And Widow Fatima Liato, in her tribute delivered on her behalf by Aminata Fofana, described her husband as a true friend, kind and star of her story.

Mr Liato who died on August 6, 2026 at the age of 61, at Maina Soko Medical Hospital has since been put to rest at Lusaka’s Leopards Hill Memorial Park.

He is survived by a wife, 13 Children and 12 Grandchildren

World.title: Copper Queens need tactical overhaul – Kaona  ‎
World.content:
Respected sports administrator Mwembe Kaona says the Copper Queens’ early exit from the 2024 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers should force a national reflection on Zambia’s tactical approach.

‎

‎Kaona said while Zambia’s women’s football has grown in talent, ambition and global presence, the tactical system has not kept pace.

‎

‎“Zambia’s women’s football has evolved in talent, ambition, and global presence, yet the tactical system guiding that talent has not kept pace. The result is a widening gap between what the Copper Queens are capable of and what their current tactical identity allows them to achieve,” he noted.

‎

‎Kaona argued that the team must move away from improvisation and emotional football to embrace a modern, structured and intelligent style.

‎

‎He cited the 6–0 victory over Egypt as proof of Zambia’s attacking potential, but said the loss to Nigeria, even after Nigeria went down to 10 players, exposed structural weaknesses.

‎

‎“Zambia’s long‑standing reliance on direct, transition‑heavy football has become predictable. Against disciplined opponents, hopeful long balls are easily neutralised, midfielders are bypassed, and the team loses control of the match tempo,” Kaona said.

‎

‎The administrator proposed that Zambia adopt a clearly defined ‘game model’ covering build-up, pressing, defending and chance creation. He said this would give the Copper Queens predictable patterns, clear roles, and consistency from youth to senior level.

‎

‎Kaona outlined key reforms: modernising build-up play, midfielders who can receive under pressure, full-backs who understand underlaps, using half-spaces as the main attacking corridor, coordinated pressing, controlled transitions, and designed set-piece routines.

‎

‎“Possession is not a luxury; it is a necessity. Against elite teams, Zambia must learn to slow the game down, stretch the pitch, and create chances through structured patterns rather than desperation,” Kaona said.

‎

‎He concluded that the WAFCON exit, while painful, could be a turning point if Zambia embraces tactical reform with seriousness and unity.

‎

‎“The Copper Queens are no longer outsiders. To match that expectation, Zambia must modernise its tactical identity. If Zambia embraces tactical reform… the Copper Queens will not only return stronger—they will redefine African women’s football.”

World.title: State House calls for peace ahead of General Elections
World.content:
State House Chief Communication Specialist, Clayson Hamasaka, has called for peace, tolerance, and honest leadership ahead of this year’s General Elections.

Mr Hamasaka emphasised that peace must be maintained through the final hours following this week’s General Election.

He highlighted that every human life is precious and stressed that any calls for taking of a human life should be treated with the gravity they deserve by all political parties.

Mr Hamasaka expressed concern over a recent incident involving former Nkana Member of Parliament, Binwell Mpundu, and Tonse Alliance President Brian Mundubile, describing them as troubling.

“Zambians are watching a leadership that cannot give straight answers about language touching on human life,” he stated.

Mr Hamasaka condemned the remarks, noting that they were initially blamed on Artificial Intelligence (AI) before an acknowledgment was made.

He urged that this is not a time for political games or contradictory explanations but a moment for political leaders to reject inflammatory language and ensure no citizen is put in danger for political gain.

“The 2026 General election will be peaceful because the Zambian people have chosen peace,” he affirmed.

This is contained in a statement issued to ZANIS today by State House Chief Communications Specialist, Clayson Hamasaka.

World.title: Govt. committed to improving the welfare of public workers
World.content:
Muchinga Province Permanent Secretary Tuesday Bwalya says government will continue to deliver infrastructure development and improve the welfare of public service workers.

Dr Bwalya reaffirmed the critical role of civil servants in policy implementation and national development.

ZANIS reports that the Permanent secretary highlighted that the country’s economy has grown to six percent from negative three percent, attributing the growth to the hard work and dedication of civil servants.

“We shall continue to invest in infrastructure development. We shall continue building more schools, we shall continue building more hospitals, clinics,” he said.

Dr Bwalya made the remarks when he addressed civil servants in Isoka and Mafinga districts.

The Permanent Secretary said as the economy continues to make gains, government will see to it that the welfare of public service workers is improved.

And Dr Bwalya urged civil servants to remain professional, support the government of the day, and not get involved in partisan politics.

In both districts, civil servants commended the government for the achievements so far stating that it is due to the policies implemented in the last five years.

Isoka Town Council Director of Finance Joseph Chanda said the government has introduced and strengthened various programmes aimed at improving the livelihoods of the people

He named some of the programmes as the enhanced Constituency Development Fund (CDF), education and skills development, health infrastructure, social protection and community empowerment.

“As we pledge our full support to government in implementing policies and programmes aimed at bringing development and improving the livelihoods of our people. We remain committed to ensuring that Government programmes are translated into tangible benefits on the ground through effective service delivery, prudent use of public resources, accountability and transparency,” he said

And Mafinga District Director Health Services John Mwiche assured that civil servants in the district will adhere to the Permanent Secretary’s guidance to uphold professionalism and be of good conduct to serve the people better.

World.title: Kabwe magistrate court adjourns case involving NRPUP candidate
World.content:
The Kabwe Magistrate court has adjourned a matter in which National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) Mayoral aspiring candidate for Kabwe, Wilson Pondamali and seven others are facing charges of being in possession of offensive weapons and unlawful assembly contrary to the law, to September 1st, 2026.

Kabwe Resident Magistrate, Gloria Chipasha, adjourned the matter after the accused failed to take plea as they were not present before the court.

The accused are Pondamali aged 53, of House No. H21, Gwembe Street in Highridge, Bright Chileshe 28, of Kamushanga Compound, Mushitu Muhamba 28, of Luansanse Area, Danny Nkhoma, whose age is not known but of Katondo Compound and Daniel Chewe 53, also of Katondo Compound.

Others are Patrick Manson Chimfwembe 22 and Sylvester Kolala 42, both of Katondo Compound in Kabwe District.

The accused persons are charged with unlawful assembly contrary to section 74(1) and 76 and with possession of offensive weapons contrary to section 85(1) of the penal code chapter 87 of the laws of Zambia.

Magistrate Chipasha adjourned the matter after the accused’s legal representative, Changano Changano of Chirwa and Associates informed her that the accused, who were supposed to take plea, were not present before the court and they are all on police bond.

Facts before the court are that in the first count, Pondamali, who is Kabwe Mayoral candidate on the NRPUP ticket in the 13th August general election and others, are alleged to have on 7th June 2026 in Kabwe district, with a common purpose of committing an offence, jointly and whilst acting together, did assemble without lawful authority.

In the second count, it is also alleged that the accused persons on the 7th June 2026 in Kabwe district, jointly and whilst acting together, had in their possession offensive articles namely stones without lawful authority.

State Prosecutor Charity Munyonga informed magistrate Chipasha that instructions from the Director of Public Prosecutions were ready but all the seven accused persons were not present before the court.

The court has since given Pondamali and his co-accused a benefit of doubt, extended their police bond and adjourned the matter to September 1, 2026 for plea.

World.title: Liberia: Boakai Names Retired Army General to Head Anti-Drug Agency
World.content:
The Executive Mansion says Ziankahn's appointment reflects the President's confidence in his "leadership, integrity, and operational experience."

President Joseph Nyuma Boakai has made perhaps his most consequential national security appointment since assuming office, naming former Defense Minister, retired Major General Daniel Dee Ziankahn, as Director General of the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA) in a move that signals a fundamental shift in the government's strategy against transnational narcotics trafficking.

The appointment comes at a defining moment for Liberia's anti-drug campaign -- one marked by record cocaine seizures, allegations of institutional infiltration by organized crime, dismissals of senior security officials, and mounting international scrutiny over whether Liberia has become an emerging transit and storage hub for global narcotics syndicates.

Rather than selecting another career drug enforcement officer, President Boakai has entrusted the agency to one of the country's most experienced military minds, suggesting that the administration increasingly views narcotics trafficking not merely as a law enforcement problem but as a national security emergency.

Ziankahn's appointment follows months of extraordinary anti-narcotics operations that have transformed Liberia's security landscape.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The crisis reached international prominence after authorities intercepted approximately 237.6 kilograms of cocaine valued at about US$19 million at Roberts International Airport earlier this year. That operation exposed what investigators described as sophisticated trafficking methods involving airport operations and triggered an extensive criminal investigation.

Only weeks later, authorities executed an even more dramatic operation in Duazon, Margibi County, where investigators seized nearly 3.97 metric tons of suspected cocaine with an estimated international street value exceeding US$370 million -- one of the largest narcotics seizures ever recorded in Liberia and among the most significant in West Africa.

The scale of both seizures fundamentally altered perceptions of Liberia's role in international narcotics trafficking.

For years, security analysts had warned that West Africa was increasingly serving as a bridge between cocaine-producing regions in Latin America and lucrative consumer markets in Europe.

The Liberian seizures appeared to reinforce those concerns, suggesting that international trafficking organizations may have established increasingly sophisticated logistical networks within the country.

The investigations that followed produced consequences extending far beyond the drug seizures themselves.

As investigators traced the alleged trafficking operations, allegations emerged suggesting that elements within the security architecture may have been compromised.

President Boakai responded with an unprecedented series of administrative actions, dismissing, suspending and ordering investigations into officials from several security institutions, including the Liberia National Police (LNP), National Security Agency (NSA), Roberts International Airport (RIA), and the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency itself.

Those measures reflected the administration's determination to demonstrate that no institution would be insulated from accountability if credible evidence of misconduct emerged.

The actions also exposed what many analysts consider the greatest institutional threat confronting the country's anti-drug campaign: the possibility that sophisticated international criminal organizations may seek to infiltrate state institutions responsible for combating them.

Such concerns are not unique to Liberia.

Across the world, transnational narcotics organizations have historically relied not only on logistical sophistication but also on corruption, insider facilitation and institutional compromise.

Why Ziankahn?

Against that backdrop, President Boakai's choice of Daniel Dee Ziankahn appears highly strategic.

Unlike many previous leaders of the LDEA, Ziankahn arrives with decades of experience in military command, institutional reform and national security planning.

During his tenure as Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of Liberia (AFL), he became widely associated with efforts to professionalize Liberia's post-war military following years of civil conflict.

Working alongside international partners, including the United States, he helped oversee reforms aimed at transforming the AFL into a disciplined, professional institution operating under democratic civilian control.

His subsequent service as Minister of National Defense further expanded his experience managing complex security institutions and coordinating with regional and international partners.

More recently, Ziankahn has served as Military Adviser to President Boakai, providing strategic advice on national and regional security matters.

His appointment therefore brings together operational military leadership, institutional reform experience and direct presidential confidence.

Unlike a conventional law enforcement appointment, it places a seasoned strategic commander at the helm of the country's principal anti-narcotics agency.

The Executive Mansion emphasized that Ziankahn's appointment reflects the President's confidence in his "leadership, integrity, and operational experience," while assigning him direct responsibility for intensifying Liberia's campaign against illicit drugs and organized crime.

The President has also appointed to the LDEA Precious Rue as Deputy Director General for Operations and Prince Mulbah as Deputy Director General for Administration, pending Senate confirmation.

All three officials have been instructed to assume their responsibilities immediately in acting capacities.

The restructuring also returns Ernest Tarpeh to the National Security Agency, while former Officer-in-Charge Fitzgerald Biago has been indefinitely suspended from the Liberia National Police over ethical concerns pending further investigation.

Although the Ministry of Justice reportedly found no evidence directly linking Biago to narcotics trafficking, President Boakai concluded that ethical issues identified in the investigation warranted additional scrutiny.

That distinction reflects the administration's emerging message: legal innocence does not necessarily preclude administrative accountability where questions of institutional integrity arise.

Ziankahn's appointment inevitably raises broader questions about the evolving character of Liberia's anti-drug campaign.

Drug enforcement agencies traditionally operate as civilian law enforcement institutions emphasizing criminal investigations, prosecutions and intelligence gathering.

By selecting a retired four-star military officer to lead the LDEA, President Boakai appears to be elevating narcotics trafficking to the level of a national security threat.

That does not necessarily imply militarization of policing.

Rather, it suggests greater emphasis on intelligence coordination, operational discipline, inter-agency cooperation and strategic planning.

The President has directed the new leadership to work closely with the Ministry of Justice, Joint Security and international partners to dismantle trafficking networks, strengthen border controls and improve intelligence capabilities.

Such coordination will likely become increasingly important as investigations continue across multiple jurisdictions.

Liberia's response carries significance beyond its borders.

International partners -- including the United States, the European Union, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), ECOWAS and INTERPOL -- closely monitor countries serving as potential transit points for narcotics trafficking.

Major cocaine seizures often become tests of institutional credibility.

Foreign governments generally assess not only whether drugs are intercepted but also whether investigations reach the criminal networks responsible and whether compromised public officials are held accountable.

Close 

Boakai's successive dismissals, suspensions and institutional reforms therefore appear designed partly to reassure international partners that Liberia remains committed to confronting organized crime despite the scale of recent challenges.

Yet appointments alone cannot dismantle sophisticated international trafficking networks.

Experts note that sustainable success will depend on broader institutional reforms, including stronger financial investigations, improved border surveillance, enhanced intelligence-sharing, witness protection mechanisms, prosecutorial capacity and judicial efficiency.

Liberia must also continue strengthening airport security, maritime surveillance and anti-money laundering systems if it hopes to disrupt the financial infrastructure sustaining organized criminal enterprises.

Equally important will be restoring public confidence in institutions that recent investigations have exposed to allegations of misconduct.

Announcing the appointments, President Boakai reaffirmed that narcotics trafficking represents one of Liberia's gravest threats to national security, public health and national development.

"Our fight against drugs is a fight for the future of Liberia," the President declared. "We will continue to strengthen our institutions, hold public officials to the highest ethical standards, and pursue those who seek to poison our communities. There will be no safe haven for drug traffickers or those who aid and abet them."

Those remarks reinforce an earlier pledge made after the first major cocaine seizure that his administration would dismantle the criminal networks operating within Liberia rather than merely seize narcotics shipments.

The assignment, for Ziankahn, may become the most demanding chapter of a career spanning military leadership, defense policy and national security.

It also represents, for the President, a high-stakes bet that disciplined leadership, institutional credibility and strategic coordination can restore confidence in an agency whose reputation has been shaken by allegations of internal compromise.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 11, 2026
World.content:
Zambia Election Set for Closely Fought Opposition Battle

Zambia's 13 August election has become a closely contested battle between the ruling United Party for National Development and the Tonse-Pamodzi opposition alliance, led by newcomer Brian Mundubile and backed by former Patriotic Front structures. The election is expected to test the opposition's strength and serve as a referendum on President Hakainde Hichilema's record. The government has made progress on debt restructuring, economic growth and inflation. But the high cost of living remains a big concern for voters. The poll is also taking place amid concerns over alleged state interference, restrictions on opposition activity and controversial legislative changes, making it a key test for Zambia's democracy.

WHO Warns DR Congo Ebola Response Falling Behind

More than 1,900 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak. 60-70% of deaths occur in communities before patients reach treatment centres. The WHO said that the concentration of healthcare services in Bunia, Ituri province, is forcing patients to travel long distances and seek care too late. Poor transport systems may also increase transmission. The agency plans to expand treatment facilities closer to communities, add 400 Ebola beds and strengthen public awareness and early referrals. WHO is also looking to the town of Aru, where no new cases have been reported for two weeks after authorities expanded surveillance and response beyond individual patients to surrounding communities.



Nigeria Lassa Fever Cases Reach 1,000 in 2026

Nigeria has reported 1,000 confirmed cases of Lassa fever and 237 deaths in 2026, with cases reported in 23 states and 116 local government areas. Five states, Ondo, Bauchi, Taraba, Edo and Benue, account for 86% of confirmed cases. At least 53 healthcare workers have also been infected, prompting the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention to introduce a 30-day protection plan for frontline staff. The agency has said that late presentation, high treatment costs, poor sanitation and limited awareness are contributing to the outbreak and high fatality rate. Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic disease transmitted primarily through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected rodents.

Malawi Land Audit Flags Irregular Plot Allocations

Malawi's Ministry of Lands is set to release findings from a pilot land ownership audit in Lilongwe that reportedly uncovered irregularities in the allocation of plots in the affluent Area 3 and Area 10. The audit was launched in February 2026 to improve transparency and accountability in land administration. It is said to have identified politically exposed individuals, including current and former ministers, judges and MPs, among those allegedly linked to irregular land acquisitions. The findings could trigger political controversy, with questions remaining over whether those implicated will be publicly named or face legal or disciplinary action.

UN Somalia Auction Raises Security Concerns

The UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) has opened a tender to auction vehicles, generators, IT equipment, medical supplies, construction machinery and other assets. This comes as Washington moves to end funding for the mission's logistical support by the end of 2026. UNSOS provides critical transport, fuel, food and other supplies to about 12,000 African troops and police serving under AUSSOM in the fight against al-Shabab. The auction has raised concerns among civil society groups over transparency and oversight. Regional leaders have warned that any premature reduction in international support could create a security vacuum as al-Shabab continues to operate in parts of Somalia.

Close 

Climate Change Shifts Africa's Malaria Risk

Climate change is reshaping malaria risk across Africa, with rising temperatures making parts of southern Africa and high-elevation areas of East Africa increasingly suitable for transmission, according to a new Nature study. Some parts of West and Central Africa may have become too hot for optimal malaria transmission. The region still bears about 95% of the global malaria burden. But experts warn that climate change is only part of the equation, with funding gaps, drug and insecticide resistance, and weak health systems still major threats. They are urging countries in emerging risk areas to step up malaria prevention and surveillance while maintaining elimination efforts in high-burden areas.

World.title: South Africa: Immigrant Traders See Their Livelihoods Destroyed By March and March
World.content:
Traders with documents and permits chased away, leaving Bellville bus terminus market almost empty

Dozens of immigrant traders who usually traded at the Golden Arrow terminus in Bellville are staying away because of anti-immigrant protests.

When we visited the once bustling site last week, it was quiet with only a handful of traders. Many stalls were deserted.

Some traders we spoke to said they had tried to set up shop in other areas but were stopped. They have not traded at the bus site since the March and March 30 June "deadline" demanding "illegal immigrants" leave South Africa.



"I need to pay rent, put food on the table, and pay the bills," a Zimbabwean man who asked to remain anonymous told GroundUp.

He said he has been selling clothes in Bellville for about five years. He left Zimbabwe in 2008 when its economy collapsed.

While he has not been directly threatened, he has witnessed others being harassed.

"They will take your stuff and throw it on the ground," he said.

"It hurts, but as much as it hurts, it's their country, and they're also marginalised people."

Another trader, who introduced herself as Meye, said she has had a permit to trade since 2010. She fled the DRC in 2003.

"We are legal; everything is correct. But they say we are foreigners and we need to go back to our country."

A single mother of three, she says she is now struggling to feed and school her children.

Another single mother, Safia, says she has been unable to trade despite having refugee status and a trading permit. She came from Somalia in 2010.

She said law enforcement needs to protect the traders better.

"I can't sleep at night because of what is happening. I can't even pay my rent. I can't support my children," she said.

Abdulhakim Husein, Western Cape director of the Somalia Association of South Africa, told GroundUp that he had been assisting traders since the start of July.

He said many asylum seekers and refugees are traders as they have to rely on being self-employed. They came from Somalia, DRC, Zimbabwe, Angola and Burundi.

He said that at a meeting on 13 July (which the City confirmed), it was agreed that traders with valid permits should be allowed to trade. But on 14 July, they received a message warning them about a March and March protest in the area.

Husein said they have approached a legal NGO for assistance.

City spokesperson Luthando Tyhalibongo said foreign nationals whose immigration status has been verified by Home Affairs are permitted to trade with a valid permit. These cost R78 per month.

Close 

"It is a concern whenever permitted traders, whether South African citizens or foreign nationals lawfully permitted to trade, are prevented from engaging in legal economic activity," he said.

He said intimidation and threats should be reported to SAPS.

World.title: South Africa: Gauteng Gets 500,000 Grade 1 and 8 Applications - South African News Briefs - August 11, 2026
World.content:
Gauteng Records Nearly 500,000 Grade 1 and 8 Applications

Almost half a million applications have been submitted for Grade 1 and Grade 8 places in Gauteng for the 2027 academic year since the online application system opened, reports EWN. The Gauteng Department of Education has said that improvements have been made to streamline the process. Education MEC Lebogang Maile has urged parents to apply early. The department also says learners awaiting specialised placement should receive interim support rather than remain on waiting lists, with officials focusing on successful placements and resolving outstanding cases.

Strong Winds Damage Homes in Free State

The South African Red Cross Society is assessing damage caused by strong winds and heavy rainfall in Koppies and other parts of the Free State, reports SABC News. Several homes have reportedly been damaged, including roofs blown off, as severe weather persists. Red Cross volunteers are working with disaster management authorities and municipalities. Assessments continue, with humanitarian assistance being provided to affected households.

Fadiel Adams Unlikely to Testify at Madlanga Commission

National Coloured Congress leader Fadiel Adams is unlikely to testify before the Madlanga Commission, reports EWN. This comes after the commission received his affidavit and supporting documents late. Adams was expected to testify about his involvement in an Investigating Directorate Against Corruption probe into alleged corruption within Crime Intelligence. In 2024, he asked IDAC to investigate claims that the Political Killings Task Team had misused secret service funds for luxury accommodation and vehicles.

World.title: Gambia: Is the Opposition Speaking With One Voice?
World.content:
Foroyaa has observed that the same opposition parties have been attending many coalition talks and have not been speaking with one voice to be able to build a political force capable of challenging and removing the incumbent. The will to build coalitions is there but the capability to do so seems to be elusive. Gambians are still wondering which coalition arrangement will end in unity rather than disunity as is evident so far in coalition arrangements that are concluded.

Any conclusion of coalition talks that ends in disunity is not good for the opposition and should be avoided at all cost. The Gambian people want a coalition that can bring unity of purpose and commitment among the opposition.

Foroyaa will continue to continue to monitor the coalition processes that are still in progress. The recently concluded one had a secretary who resigned prior to the conclusion of the talks. Foroyaa will find out how many stakeholders attended the talks and how many were left in the end and what the rules of engagement were and how they concluded without keeping everybody onboard.

World.title: Nigeria: 10 Police Officers, Two Civilians Killed in Kebbi Battle With Bandits
World.content:
Kebbi police said at least 17 suspected bandits were also killed after officers intercepted a heavily armed group along the Rafin Makuku axis of Sakaba LGA.

Ten police officers and two civilians were killed on Monday at a battle with suspected bandits along the Rafin Makuku axis of Sakaba Area of Kebbi State, the police have said.

Two other officers were injured in the confrontation, while the police said at least 17 suspected bandits were killed.



The police spokesperson in Kebbi, Bashir Usman, told PREMIUM TIMES that the encounter occurred at about 9:25 a.m. on 10 August after the police intercepted the armed group moving between Zamfara and Kebbi states.

"Several of the attackers were neutralised, with at least 17 suspected bandits so far assessed to have been neutralised," Mr Usman said.

He added that four motorcycles belonging to the attackers were burnt during the encounter.

The police spokesperson cautioned that the casualty figure remained subject to further verification.

"Tragically, we lost 10 gallant police personnel in the engagement, while two others sustained injuries and are receiving medical attention. Two civilians also lost their lives during the encounter," he said.

Mr Usman said the police were supporting the families of the deceased, caring for the injured officers and continuing operations against members of the armed group who fled the area.

He said further information would be released as the authorities verified details of the confrontation.

Armed group moving towards Kebbi

The deadly confrontation followed reports that a large group of armed men had moved from neighbouring Zamfara State towards communities in Kebbi.

On Monday, reports said the Air Component of Operation FANSAN YAMMA carried out airstrikes against an armed group detected moving from the Sangeko Gap in Zamfara towards the Makuku area of Kebbi.

The exact number of fighters struck has not been independently established. Some reports estimated that the group comprised more than 200 armed men travelling on motorcycles.

Security authorities have not publicly confirmed that estimate.

The air operation reportedly followed intelligence about the movement of the armed group across the inter-state corridor.

It was not immediately clear whether the airstrikes occurred before or after the confrontation in which the 10 police officers were killed.

Close 

Reported police SITREP

Separately, SaharaReporters reported on Tuesday that it obtained a police situation report concerning the Makuku incident.

The newspaper said the document identified the 10 officers killed as personnel of the 44 Police Mobile Force, Abuja, who were on special duty in the area.

It also reported that the document said police weapons and ammunition were taken following the confrontation.

PREMIUM TIMES has not independently obtained the situation report, and the Kebbi police command's statement to this newspaper did not confirm the reported loss of weapons.

The command also did not disclose the identities of the officers killed in its statement.

The police said follow-up operations were continuing against members of the armed group who fled after the encounter.

World.title: Kenya: U.S. Pledges $242mn for Ebola Response As Kenya Strengthens Regional Preparedness
World.content:
Nairobi — The United States has announced an additional $242 million to support immediate Ebola response, preparedness and humanitarian efforts in countries affected by or at risk from the outbreak in East and Central Africa.

The funding comes as health authorities across the region step up surveillance, laboratory testing, infection prevention and control measures following the outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease, a form of Ebola disease, in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda.

The US says it remains the largest financial contributor to the international Ebola response, with its support focused not only on containing active infections but also on strengthening health systems in countries such as Kenya that are at risk because of their proximity to affected areas and their role as regional transport hubs.



The latest funding will support emergency response operations, disease surveillance, medical supplies, laboratory capacity, infection prevention and control, risk communication and other preparedness measures.

According to the US government, its assistance to date has enabled 8.6 million health screenings across affected and at-risk countries and reached more than one million people with Ebola risk-communication messages.

The US has also supported more than 180 health facilities in Ebola-affected areas and directly operated 12 specialised facilities in the Democratic Republic of Congo for the isolation and treatment of Ebola patients.

Nearly 300 metric tonnes of critical supplies have been procured and distributed under the response, including personal protective equipment and commodities required for water, sanitation, hygiene and infection prevention and control.

The assistance has also helped strengthen diagnostic capacity at 11 operational laboratories across the region.

Kenya has emerged as a key part of the regional preparedness strategy because of its extensive air and road links with Uganda, the Democratic Republic of Congo and other countries in the region.

The country has strengthened screening at points of entry, surveillance and laboratory preparedness while identifying isolation and treatment facilities capable of handling suspected cases.

The government has designated specialised Ebola isolation and treatment facilities at Kenyatta National Hospital, Kenya National Police Hospital and Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital, while additional response sites have been identified in high-risk border counties.

The United States has also been supporting Kenya's broader emergency preparedness infrastructure. Through the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the partnership has helped establish 25 county Public Health Emergency Operations Centres, strengthening the country's ability to detect, coordinate and respond to disease outbreaks. The centres have already been used to respond to more than 100 public-health events, including malaria, dengue and rabies.

The current Ebola response has given those systems an additional test as Kenya seeks to ensure that suspected cases can be detected, isolated and investigated before transmission occurs.

The US has separately been involved in plans for a temporary Ebola quarantine facility at a Kenyan military installation in Laikipia County, intended primarily for Americans exposed to Ebola while working in the region.

The proposed facility, reported to have a capacity of about 50 beds, became the subject of legal challenges and public protests, with opponents questioning the arrangements under which Kenya would host potentially exposed American citizens. A Kenyan court temporarily halted the plans, while the government was ordered to provide further details about the proposed facility.

The controversy has nevertheless highlighted the wider importance of Kenya's preparedness as the region confronts recurring outbreaks of highly infectious diseases.

In June, Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale said construction-related activities at the Laikipia site had been halted following a court order. Reuters reported that the facility was intended to support the isolation of Americans potentially exposed to Ebola in the region.

The current outbreak is particularly significant because it involves the Bundibugyo virus, one of the viruses that causes Ebola disease. Unlike the Zaire strain, for which an approved vaccine exists, there is currently no approved vaccine specifically for Bundibugyo virus. Treatment relies largely on intensive supportive care, making early detection, isolation and infection prevention critical.

Close 

The outbreak began in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo and subsequently spread to Uganda. The US CDC says its response has included disease surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory sample collection and sequencing, infection prevention and control, border health measures, and risk communication.

For Kenya, the emphasis is therefore on preventing importation while ensuring that any suspected case can be quickly identified and safely managed.

The US says the new $242 million commitment will help maintain that regional response while strengthening health systems so that countries can detect and contain outbreaks before they cross borders.

The latest intervention also reflects the broader lesson from previous Ebola outbreaks: containing the disease at its source and ensuring neighbouring countries have functioning surveillance, laboratories, trained health workers and adequate protective equipment are central to preventing a local outbreak from becoming a regional crisis.

World.title: Nigeria: Troops Repel Iswap Attack On Borno Base, Kill Many Terrorists
World.content:
Troops of the Joint Task Force, North East, Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have repelled a midnight attack by the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists on a Forward Operating Base (FOB) in Gajiram, Nganzai LGA of Borno State.

The coordinated assault, which took place at around 12:20 am on Monday, saw the insurgents attempt to overrun the military installation.

However, vigilant troops stood their ground, engaging the terrorists in a fierce firefight.

According to a statement issued by the Acting Media Information Officer for the operation, Captain Mohammed Goni, the troops responded with overwhelming and sustained firepower, forcing the heavily armed attackers to retreat in disarray after suffering severe casualties.

"During the engagement, troops neutralised several of the terrorists and recovered weapons, ammunition and communication gadgets," he said.

According to him, post-battle surveillance footage reviewed by military intelligence confirmed that the fleeing terrorists evacuated numerous dead and wounded fighters as they scrambled back into the night.

Goni said the recovered equipment and surveillance materials are currently undergoing further operational assessment.

Despite the decisive victory, Goni said the attack came at a cost, as a portion of the base's defensive position was temporarily breached during the intense exchange, resulting in injuries to some soldiers.

He, however, noted that the wounded personnel are currently receiving medical attention.

World.title: Parents speak out after son with autism, 6, was suspended for biting sandwich into shape of gun
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The parents of a Georgia first-grader with autism are speaking out after their son was suspended for biting his sandwich into the shape of a gun and pointing it at a classmate during lunch, arguing that the school's strict disciplinary policies fail to account for his developmental disabilities.

John Medina, 6, was suspended last March while in first grade at Sarah Harp Elementary School in Fayette County, south of Atlanta. He was diagnosed with level 1 autism at age 4 and later diagnosed with ADHD, conditions his parents say can make it difficult for him to understand social norms.

In an interview with Fox News Digital, parents Kristin and Juan "Ricky" Medina said that John is exceptionally advanced academically, but the school's apparent strict policies and initial lack of developmental assistance have led to roughly 15 suspensions and more than two dozen disciplinary actions since 2023. They added that while some incidents justified escalation, other harmless acts, such as hunting drawings and hand-gun gestures, have also drawn school discipline and scrutiny.

The disciplinary history has ultimately taken a toll on John's self-esteem, especially as he already struggles to make friends and often feels isolated, his parents said. They said their son refers to himself as a "bad kid" because of how he feels he is treated by his peers and the school environment.

10-YEAR-OLD BOY RECOUNTS NEAR-DROWNING AS FAMILY REVEALS FRIENDSHIP WITH CALIFORNIA TEEN LIFEGUARD HERO

Kristin said she was initially shocked to learn that John had been suspended over the sandwich incident, questioning the school's reported "strike" system, in which minor actions such as making a hand gesture or saying the word "gun" can escalate to suspension.

"It was upsetting for me to hear that it was, that is what he was getting in trouble for," Kristin said.

"I felt like they were cracking down more on small stuff, you know, stuff that maybe he didn't need to be suspended for," Ricky added.

While John has been involved in physical incidents, including pushing another student in PE and hitting a classmate with a branch, his parents said many official disciplinary actions stemmed from what they considered harmless hand gestures. Other standard behaviors, like drawing a pilgrim shooting a turkey for Thanksgiving, also drew intense school scrutiny, they said.

They added that weapon-related topics are specifically not discussed in their home, but said they cannot control the outside influences John encounters. They added that children can naturally develop an imaginative fascination with weapons, but John’s autism makes it more difficult for him to filter his speech in the way other children might.

MONTANA TEEN THROWS LASSO TO MAN IN YELLOWSTONE RIVER IN SPLIT-SECOND RESCUE

They also stressed that, because of his autism, traditional punishments are ineffective and could inadvertently reinforce the idea that saying the word "gun" will allow him to leave school when he is having a bad day.

"Instead of singling him out, just make it a teachable moment for him. Teach, ‘Hey, we don't do this in school because of this reason, it's not appropriate,’" Kristin said.

However, the family said they initially faced pushback from the school over developmental accommodations. Kristin said the school initially refused to grant John an Individualized Education Program (IEP), because he was too academically advanced and officials "didn't see" his autism.

According to Kristin, it took about a year and a half, 10 to 12 suspensions and a second evaluation that resulted in an ADHD diagnosis before the school approved his IEP.

John’s parents said they worry that repeatedly focusing on what they consider harmless childhood behavior has reinforced a negative self-image and made him increasingly eager to leave school. John is hesitant to attend school because he believes people are "going to laugh at him for making wrong choices," his parents said.

"I just want to see John start to get his self-esteem built up, his confidence built up, friendships built up," Kristin said. "I don't want him to continue to feel singled out."

The parents said John thankfully finished the previous school year strong, reading at a third-grade level and coming just four test points short of qualifying for the gifted and talented program.

The school also appeared to ease up on suspensions recently, particularly after the family hired Donna Reynolds, a special education advocate, to represent them during school meetings.

John is also currently on a behavioral plan that includes an aide during unstructured periods, including lunch, recess and PE. He also spends time in a smaller, calmer classroom setting, where his parents said he performs exceptionally well.

"What I want to see is that there's less severe punishment like suspensions," Ricky said. "And just continue to talk through things so you can have opportunities to learn from things and maybe focus on real serious concerns."

Fox News Digital reached out to Fayette County Public Schools, the school district under which John's school falls, about his situation. The district declined to go into specific details, but encouraged a review of John's "complete disciplinary history and the full context surrounding the situation rather than focusing on one isolated event."

The parents of University of Idaho student Kaylee Goncalves opened up about the daily reality of losing their daughter, revealing their morning thoughts and nightly prayers since her murder.

"The first thing every single morning I often ask myself: Is this going to be forever? Will this eventually end? Will it eventually, will it not be the first thing that I think about when I open my eyes?" Kristi told host Sean Hannity.

KAYLEE GONCALVES' MOTHER SAYS FAMILY READY FOR TRIAL AFTER BRYAN KOHBERGER SEEKS TO WITHDRAW GUILTY PLEA

"But at this point I've learned that it's just the new way of life," she added.

Kaylee Goncalves was one of four University of Idaho students killed in November 2022. Bryan Kohberger pleaded guilty in July 2025 to four counts of first-degree murder and one count of felony burglary as part of a deal that spared him the death penalty. He has since sought to withdraw his guilty plea.

Goncalves' father, Steve, added that every night, Kristi hopes their daughter visits her in her dreams so she can tell Kaylee she loves her.

"First and foremost, before she goes to bed, she's praying that Kaylee comes and visits her. She wants to have a conversation. She wants to talk to her. She wants to tell her she loves her. She wants to say everything that we can't say," Steve said.

"Then if you don't have that dream, you wake up disappointed that you didn't have a dream about your baby and had that conversation, and then you just try to fake through it," he added.

Kohberger is now seeking to withdraw the guilty plea that spared him the death penalty for the murders of Goncalves, Madison Mogen, Ethan Chapin and Xana Kernodle. He was sentenced to four consecutive life sentences in prison without the possibility of parole, plus 10 years for burglary.

The Goncalves family said Kohberger's attempt to withdraw his plea has been difficult for them after years of legal proceedings, but Kristi Goncalves said his latest challenge could provide another opportunity for prosecutors to pursue the death penalty.

World.title: Former Wisconsin Gov Scott Walker warns Hong ‘undermining one of her strengths’ with campaign backtracking

EXCLUSIVE — Former Wisconsin Gov. Scott Walker shared his concerns about politics in the state amid the rise of democratic socialist Francesca Hong, while also arguing she's "undermining" her own campaign in a Fox News Digital interview on Tuesday.

Hong, a Wisconsin state representative, is leading the field heading into Tuesday's Democratic primary, according to recent polling. The far-left, 37-year-old former chef and single mother has courted controversy in recent weeks for her progressive platform and past rhetoric about abolishing the police, as well as her hot take on Thanksgiving.

"Cancel Thanksgiving. Should have done this in 1621," Hong wrote in a now-deleted November 2020 post to X. "If it takes a worldwide pandemic for us to realize we should stop celebrating colonialism and the original superspreader event that killed indigenous folx [sic] and women, so be it," she added. She has since said her views have "evolved," telling Politico Thanksgiving is actually her "favorite" holiday.

"Well one, I think it’s a sign she’ll say just about anything to get elected," Walker, who is now the president of Young America's Foundation, told Fox News Digital ahead of Tuesday’s primary. "And finally, as she’s getting close, thinking she might actually be the nominee, people are telling her you cannot have outrageously outlandish ideas."

WISCONSIN DEM SOCIALIST GUBERNATORIAL HOPEFUL DODGES WHETHER SHE STILL WANTS TO 'ABOLISH POLICE'

"Not only on Thanksgiving. Doesn’t care for Christmas. Heck, in Wisconsin, doesn’t like Culver’s cheese curds," Walker said, in reference to another of Hong's old social media posts. "Those are all things that are wildly out of touch with the people that she’s going to need if she’s got a shot for the general election."

Walker warned Hong, however, that she could be hurting her campaign because primary voters had been attracted to her, in part, because of her bucking of the Democratic establishment.

"But I think she’s undermining one of her strengths," Walker said. "One of the reasons why she’s going to win today’s primary is because Democratic primary voters view her as not the establishment, not the traditional politician. Someone who will just tell it like it is, even if people don’t agree with her. So the more she backtracks on things she didn’t even say as a kid — she’s actually posted as an elected official — the more I think she starts to undermine her own base, and the typical voter can see right through her."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Hong campaign for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Walker is the most recent Republican to serve as Wisconsin governor. He was elected in 2010 and 2014 — and also survived a recall in 2012 — before losing to Democrat Tony Evers during a bid for a third term in 2018.

SOCIALIST FRONTRUNNER IN THE HOT SEAT AFTER 'CANCEL THANKSGIVING' POST EMERGES ONLINE

Establishment Democrats have been hoping to stop Hong in her tracks, but she's the clear polling favorite going into Tuesday night. David Crowley, the Milwaukee County executive who earned the endorsement of outgoing Gov. Evers, told Politico that Republicans wanted Hong to be their opponent.

"You know, it’s the only time that I know that the governor — Tony Evers — the Republican Governors Association and Turning Point USA have ever been on the same page: in thinking that Francesca Hong is the best candidate to lose this race," Crowley said.

Whoever wins Tuesday's Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial primary will face Trump ally Tom Tiffany, who is heavily favored in the Republican primary.

Hong has pushed back on the narrative that she’s too extreme, although she has conspicuously failed to win the endorsement of even far-left darling Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt.

"We have to take this moment, a movement moment, and be bold with transformative change, and build the actual big tent that we can, and we must be as Democrats," Hong told a crowd at a senior community center in Siren.

"It’s common sense versus dangerously crazy," Walker told Fox News Digital of the recent rise of democratic socialism in the U.S. "When you talk about abolishing the police, when you talk about a world without prisons, no consequences for criminals, no push for public safety."

SCOTT WALKER: DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE COMING FOR MY STATE. THIS IS HOW WE BEAT THEM

SCOTT WALKER: DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE COMING FOR MY STATE. THIS IS HOW WE BEAT THEM

Walker said it is intriguing timing that next year will be the 40th anniversary of President Ronald Reagan’s "Tear down this wall" speech at the Berlin Wall.

"In all the years since, I think we’ve kind of lost a sense in America, of why there was a wall there in the first place, why did it have to come down," he said. "That’s because communism and democratic socialism are barriers to freedom. They’re barriers to economic freedom, political freedom, even religious freedom. That’s why Ronald Reagan, Pope John Paul II, Margaret Thatcher and others fought so hard to bring that down. We have to remind anyone, but particularly young people, that democratic socialism has failed in Venezuela, just like communism failed in the old Soviet Union. And it’s a really important reminder."

Walker said the newfound popularity of democratic socialism is in part due to primary voters shifting to the left, particularly under President Donald Trump. Second, he said, is the "years of liberal indoctrination on college campuses." The third, he argued, is due to a strong frustration over housing prices and the feeling that young adults' "piece of the American dream is slipping away," so they are drifting toward the extremes on either side of the aisle.

World.title: Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs chooses former Republican as running mate in re-election bid
World.content:
Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs has chosen a former Republican as her running mate for her re-election bid this November.

On Tuesday, Hobbs named John Giles, who served as a GOP mayor of Mesa, Arizona, from 2014 to 2025, as her pick for lieutenant governor.

In a joint video announcement with Giles, Hobbs said she has fought for Arizonans as governor by cutting taxes, securing the border and supporting public safety.

“Now, for the first time in our state’s history, we are electing a governor and lieutenant governor on the same ticket. And the first thing I looked for in a running mate was someone who shares that value of putting Arizonans ahead of partisan politics,” Hobbs said.

Giles said, “I was a lifelong Republican before becoming an independent because extremists shouldn’t stand in the way of getting things done.”

Giles changed his party affiliation to independent in May and voted in the Democratic primary last month, Hobbs’ communications director Michael Beyer confirmed to NBC News.

Voters will elect a lieutenant governor for the first time this fall after a ballot measure creating the position was approved in the 2022 election.

The New York Times was first to report on Hobbs’ plans.

Hobbs faces a competitive race against Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., who previously chaired the conservative House Freedom Caucus and has served in Congress since 2017. Biggs has selected former state lawmaker Sine Kerr as his running mate. Biggs won the Republican primary last month, beating fellow Rep. David Schweikert and businessmen Scott Neely and Ken Miceli.

While mayor of Mesa, Giles endorsed then-Vice President Kamala Harris for president in the 2024 election and spoke at the Democratic National Convention in Chicago that year about his disappointment with the Republican Party.

“I’m a lifelong Republican, so I feel a little out of place tonight. But I feel more at home here than in today’s Republican Party,” Giles said in his remarks. “The Grand Old Party has been kidnapped by extremists and devolved into a cult — the cult of Donald Trump.”

He added: “I have an urgent message for the majority of Americans who, like me, are in the political middle. John McCain’s Republican Party is gone, and we don’t owe a damn thing to what’s been left behind.”

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report rated the governor’s race as leaning Democratic in the battleground state, which President Donald Trump carried in 2016 and 2024 and Joe Biden won in 2020.

In 2022, Hobbs defeated Republican Kari Lake in the gubernatorial election by less than 1 percentage point. Before serving as governor, Hobbs was Arizona’s secretary of state. She also has been the minority leader in the state Senate and a member of the state House.

Hobbs recently formed a coalition of former and current Republican and independent leaders who support her re-election, which included Giles and more than 50 other business leaders and officials.

The Democratic incumbent has touted her record of working across the aisle, including signing more than 900 pieces of bipartisan legislation into law, according to her campaign. She has also highlighted her efforts to expand affordable housing and secure the border and her repeal of the state’s 1864 near-total abortion ban.

World.title: Former Marine held in Russia for more than 4 years has been released
World.content:
A former U.S. Marine who spent more than four years in a Russian prison and is believed to be seriously ill has been released and was on his way back to the United States on Tuesday.

President Donald Trump announced the release on Truth Social, saying Robert Gilman, 32, was freed after he discussed the case with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Trump said Gilman, a teacher, was released “very much on a Humanitarian Basis,” with no exchange of prisoners having taken place. He is expected to land at Andrews Air Force Base in Washington, D.C.

The president added in his post that he had spoken to Gilman “and he had one request — A GREAT cheeseburger when he lands. I will take care of that!”

The Russian government has not commented on the release.

Robert Gilman during a hearing in Voronezh, Russia in September 2024. Andrey Arhipov / Sputnik via AP

About 50 days ago, Gilman was diagnosed with a “dissociative stupor — a condition where he is non-responsive and unable to interact or eat,” Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., said in a statement following the man’s release.

“He was essentially catatonic and also suffered a severe case of pneumonia,” added Markey, who has been campaigning for Gilman’s release. “We don’t yet know the full details of his current condition or the long-term impact on his recovery.”

Gilman’s sister Lexie Hudson thanked Trump in a statement issued by Global Reach, an advocacy group representing his family.

“There is no other reason that Robert is alive today other than that President Trump heard about the case and took action,” she said.

“I am looking forward to seeing Robert. I haven’t been able to speak with him once since this all began,” she added. “We will make sure that he gets the treatment and support that he needs.”

00:21 Russia releases former Marine after four years in prison 00:00 00:00

Before his release, Hudson said in a statement on Sunday that she was worried that he would die if he wasn’t freed. “I’m more afraid for my brother than I have been since this horrible nightmare started,” she said in the statement issued by Global Reach.

Her comments on Sunday came around a month after Russia’s Kommersant newspaper reported that Gilman had been ​admitted to a hospital. Quoting his lawyer Irina Brazhnikova, the business daily reported that he was receiving treatment but it was too early to talk about a diagnosis.

Gilman, who served in the Marines from August 2019 until August 2020, had been detained in 2022. He was initially handed a 3 ½— year sentence for beating a police officer after being taken off a train for causing a disturbance.

While serving his sentence, in October 2024 Gilman was accused of attacking a prison inspector during a cell check, beating an investigator and assaulting a guard; he was sentenced to eight years and one month.

Last year, his sentence was extended again to 10 years after he was found guilty of assaulting prison guards.

Gilman’s American supporters contend he was ill when he was first arrested and also that he was provoked while in prison into actions that led to further charges.

According to Markey, Gilman was “subjected to physical torture, forced medication, and provocations by Russian authorities,” throughout his detention.

“There is no doubt that his treatment by Russian authorities is the reason Robert is in this precarious state today,” he added.

Gilman was one of at least 10 Americans known to be imprisoned in Russia.

World.title: The most dramatic meteor shower of the summer peaks the day of a solar eclipse
World.content:
One of the year’s brightest and most popular meteor showers peaks this week, offering a chance to see shooting stars cross a particularly dark sky, thanks to the new moon.

The Perseid meteor shower has been underway since mid-July, but is expected to peak overnight from Wednesday to Thursday.

Because the moon’s illuminated side is currently facing the sun, with its night side facing Earth, bright moonlight won’t interfere with one of the most anticipated skywatching events of the summer.

The Perseids’ peak coincides fortuitously with what is perhaps the season’s most eagerly awaited celestial event: a total solar eclipse that will be visible from Spain, a small part of Portugal, Greenland, Iceland and northern Russia on Wednesday.

A total solar eclipse happens when the sun, moon and Earth align and the moon passes in front of the sun, fully obscuring its light.

In locations where the eclipse will occur around sunset, people may see Perseid meteors during totality, the minutes when the moon fully blocks the sun’s light, leaving a fiery ring and temporarily darkening the skies.

The Perseids are typically one of the most popular meteor showers of the year because of their timing during warm summer months in the Northern Hemisphere (typically from around mid-July to late August) and its high rate of shooting stars. Under ideal conditions — clear weather and dark skies — the Perseids can produce as many as 100 shooting stars per hour.

Though the highest rate comes during the shower’s peak, shooting stars should continue to be visible over the next two weeks.

The Perseid meteor shower occurs when Earth passes through a cloud of dust particles and debris left over from a comet known as 109P/Swift-Tuttle, which was discovered in 1862. The streaks of light are created as the debris hits the atmosphere. The Perseids are known to produce fireballs, which are extra bright meteors that leave behind glowing trails as they disintegrate.

To see the Perseids from the Northern Hemisphere, the best timing is in the early hours before dawn. People should choose an unobstructed location under the darkest possible skies, away from city lights and other forms of light pollution.

NASA recommends letting your eyes adjust to the darkness for 20 to 30 minutes, then to sit back, look up and patiently wait for the shooting stars.

For most places in the Southern Hemisphere, the meteor shower’s radiant — the point in the sky from which the shooting stars appear to originate — won’t rise above the horizon, making them difficult to see.

NASA plans to host a virtual watch party on YouTube beginning at 12 a.m. ET Thursday, with a stream of live views from sky cameras at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama.
