World.title: One year after Putin-Trump summit, ‘spirit of Anchorage’ dissipated
World.content:
Moscow – In the year since Donald Trump hosted Vladimir Putin on US soil for a summit designed to broker an end to Russia’s offensive on Ukraine, the diplomatic initiative has fizzled out and the conflict has escalated.

For months, Russian officials talked up the “spirit of Anchorage” — a supposed climate of detente, renewed dialogue with Washington and a framework for finding a way out of the deadliest European conflict since World War II.

Now there are few traces of that atmosphere. US mediation efforts are at a standstill, both Russia and Ukraine are ramping up attacks and more civilians are being killed than at any point since the first months of the war.

– ‘Ending the war’-

On August 15, 2025, Trump broke with the West’s policy of isolating Putin, rolling out the red carpet as the Kremlin chief stepped off his plane at the Elmendorf-Richardson air base in Alaska.

It remains unclear what was decided or discussed behind closed doors.

Russia has always maintained some kind of understanding on a peace deal was struck — “a compromise proposal”, as Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov called it.

Washington has rebuffed any talk of a deal being reached.

“There was a proposal in Alaska, but there was no agreement. If there had been an agreement, we would have had an end of the war,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in June.

Moscow had hoped the summit would lay the foundations for a “lasting peace” by addressing what it calls the “root causes” of the conflict, said political analyst Sergei Markov — designated a “foreign agent” but still close to the Russian authorities.

For years — including right before launching its offensive in February 2022 — Russia has called for a new overarching security deal with the United States over Europe, NATO and arms control.

The “compromise” Russia tabled in Alaska, Markov told AFP, was to limit its territorial claims on Ukraine to the eastern Donbas region in exchange for recognition of Russia’s new borders by Washington and the lifting of sanctions.

– Disenchantment –

Those Russian demands were included in a 28-point document drafted by the United States — later cut down to 19 — after separate negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow.

The document was never published officially and never came to fruition.

US-brokered direct talks between Russia and Ukraine in early 2026 broke down, chiefly over the issue of territory.

Ukraine refuses to cede land it still controls and wants an immediate ceasefire along the current front line, with territorial status to be decided during fuller peace talks.

And since late February, Washington’s attention has been consumed by the war on Iran.

Trump has since issued fresh sanctions on Russia and the last remaining nuclear arms control agreement — New Start — has been allowed to lapse.

Having once sensed a window of opportunity to press its demands and been at pains to praise Trump’s efforts, Russia has lately allowed itself to publicly question Washington’s commitment to diplomacy.

“I don’t even want to imagine that Alaska … was conceived to gain time in order to strengthen Ukraine militarily,” Lavrov said in June.

A meeting between Lavrov and Rubio in Manila in July — their first since September 2025 — lasted only around 30 minutes.

“We’ll have to find new suggestions and new ideas” that both “Russia and Ukraine can agree to,” Rubio said after that meeting.

“That’s going to require a lot of work,” he added.

– Escalation –

The two sides’ conditions for peace are irreconcilable.

Russia demands territory alongside political and military concessions that Ukraine rejects as capitulation.

At the same time, both are convinced force can improve their negotiating position.

“The Russian armed forces will continue their mission to liberate the Donbas and Novorossiya in line with the approved plan,” Russia’s army chief Valery Gerasimov told Putin in a televised meeting in early July — referring to land stretching across eastern and southern Ukraine.

Buoyed by European support, Kyiv is banking on its long-range strike campaign to tip Russia’s economy and society over the edge.

Its attacks triggered a nationwide fuel crisis over the summer, and have forced Moscow-installed authorities to put the annexed Crimean peninsula under a local “state of emergency”.

Russia has upped its missile attacks on Kyiv, killing dozens there in recent weeks.

It has also brought Ukrainian exports through the Black Sea to a standstill through a campaign of port and ship strikes.

“The spirit of Anchorage has dissipated,” said Russian political analyst Fyodor Lukyanov — close to the ruling elite — in August.

The result? “Brutal escalation.”

World.title: Scrap all existing inter-state border check posts within six months, parl panel to transport ministry
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre should scrap all existing inter-state border check posts within six months and replace the All India Tourist Permit with a unified All India Passenger Permit within a year, a parliamentary panel has recommended, pitching for a sweeping overhaul of the countryâs bus transport system.

The committee headed by JD(U) MP Sanjay Kumar Jha made the recommendations after consultations with govt departments, bus operators, passengers and other stakeholders to identify key hurdles facing the sector, which transports more passengers daily than Indian Railways.

The panel noted that India has around 4.4 lakh buses, but only about 1.1 lakh are owned by govt entities, mainly state road transport undertakings.

Ten states account for nearly 90% of these govt-owned buses, including Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.

Calling for an overhaul of the permit regime, panel urged road transport ministry to replace the All India Tourist Permit with an All India Passenger Permit. The new permit should reflect the number of passengers actually carried, ensuring that enforcement does not hinge on whether a traveller qualifies as a âtouristâ.





âThe rights of the permit holder, including the right to halt, to board and set down passengers at notified points, and to enter public terminals on payment, should be stated exhaustively on the face of the permit,â panel said.

It also asked Centre to prevail upon six states to close border check posts that they are still operating.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Panel further recommended that all bus terminals provide private operators ânon-discriminatory accessâ to pick up passengers on payment of an entry fee, following the model at Delhiâs ISBT.

It also proposed establishment of a National Bus Terminals Authority to develop and standardise terminal infrastructure and, where states agree, manage bus terminals and intermodal passenger hubs.

Panel further recommended a unified online ticketing platform covering state-run and private bus operators for passenger convenience.

It has proposed a citizen vigilance channel, modelled on Election Commissionâs cVIGIL app, allowing passengers to file geo-tagged, time-stamped complaintsâwith photos or videosâabout overloading, unsafe transport of schoolchildren, faulty safety equipment and poor sanitation in buses, terminals and halting points.

Complaints would be automatically forwarded to the enforcement authority concerned for action within a prescribed timeframe, it said.

World.title: FSSAI tightens pan masala packaging norms; bans plastic, foil and synthetic laminates
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India's food safety regulator has barred the use of plastic and plastic-laminated packaging for pan masala, under an amendment aimed at tightening existing packaging norms, according to a press release.

The

(FSSAI) has specified that pan masala may now only be packaged in paper, paperboard, cellulose, or other naturally derived materials. Such materials must be entirely free of plastic, including polyethene, polypropylene, polyester, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and other synthetic polymers, copolymers or laminates, as well as aluminium foil or metallised layers, the release said. Tin and glass containers continue to be permitted, it added.

The press release further stated that packaging will also need to conform to clauses (f) and (i) of sub-rule 1 of rule 4 of the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, framed under the Environment Protection Act, 1986.

The amendment has been incorporated as a new entry in Schedule IV of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018, which lists suggested packaging materials. It has been placed right after the existing entries at Serial Number 10, the release said.

Notified as the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Amendment Regulations, 2026, the amendment will come into force from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette, according to the release.

The regulations were issued by FSSAI in exercise of powers conferred under clause (k) of sub-section (2) of Section 92 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and with prior approval of the Central Government, the release said.

World.title: 70 dead, 204 roads blocked: Himachal Pradesh reels under monsoon fury; damage tops Rs 910 crore
World.content:
Car lies damaged after falling rocks and debris from a hillside hit it following continuous heavy rainfall in the Anni area of Kullu

70 disaster deaths, public property damage crosses Rs 910 crore

204 roads blocked, power and water infrastructure hit

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Heavy monsoon rains continued to disrupt life across Himachal Pradesh, with 204 roads blocked, 70 people killed in rain-related incidents and damage to public property estimated at more than Rs 910 crore over the past 43 days, according to the latest State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC) assessment.The assessment covers the period from June 30 to August 11 and captures the impact of repeated heavy rainfall, landslides, cloudbursts and other weather-related incidents across the hill state.According to SEOC data, 70 people have died in direct disaster-related incidents since June 30. Landslides accounted for 14 deaths, while 23 people died after falling from steep slopes, rocks or trees. Seven deaths were caused by snake bites, six by electrocution and four by cloudbursts.Lahaul and Spiti reported the highest number of direct disaster-related deaths at 14, followed by Kangra with 12.The wider toll has also been compounded by road accidents. As many as 93 people have died in road accidents during the same period, with Chamba reporting 16 fatalities, followed by Kullu (13), Sirmaur (12) and Shimla (11), as reproted by ANI.Meanwhile, cumulative damage to public property has reached around Rs 910.35 crore.The Public Works Department has suffered the biggest losses, estimated at Rs 686.36 crore, while damage to the power sector stands at around Rs 203.90 crore.The monsoon has also damaged houses, other private structures, livestock and crops across the state's 12 districts, adding to losses for affected households.Mandi is the worst affected in terms of road connectivity, with 80 roads currently blocked. The Mandi-Kullu route has also been disrupted at Jalogi Dwada. Kullu has reported 56 blocked roads, while 23 roads remain closed in Sirmaur. Two national highways â NH-154 and NH-21 â are also among the affected routes.The road closures have disrupted inter-district connectivity and complicated the movement of essential supplies and emergency response teams.The monsoon has also damaged the state's power and drinking water infrastructure. Forty-five distribution transformer regions are currently out of service, including 41 in Sirmaur's Nahan subdivision.Around 82 drinking water supply schemes have been affected across the state. Sirmaur accounts for 31 of the disrupted schemes, followed by Hamirpur with 11 and Mandi with eight.Authorities and emergency response teams are continuing restoration work, including clearing landslides and debris, reopening roads and restoring power and water supply. However, persistent rainfall and the risk of further landslides continue to hamper relief and restoration efforts.

World.title: Army opens its establishments to students through 43 internship projects this year
World.content:
The programme offers a stipend of up to Rs 75,000 that will be disbursed upon the successful completion of the internship

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian Army has opened its establishments to student interns through the second edition of the Indian Army Internship Programme (IAIP) hosted on the AICTE national internship portal and has expanded this programme this year by adding 43 specialised projects.The programme offers a stipend of up to Rs 75,000 that will be disbursed upon the successful completion of the internship and fulfillment of all program requirements. The final stipend amount will be based on the internâs overall attendance during the period.The internships cover AI, cybersecurity, robotics, drones and counter-drone systems, hospital information systems, wargaming and simulation, and strategic communication. Through this internship programme, Indian Army envisions creating a strong ecosystem where education, technology and national service converge to prepare the next generation of innovators. The internship offers an opportunity to gain hands-on experience and professional exposure with the Army.The Army started the pilot project in May 2025. The specialised tech-infusion trials, which began in 2025 focusing on wargaming, simulation and niche research, has now expanded into a structured multi-project initiative across army directorates offering up to 43 specialised tracks.The Army has already received over 77,000 applications since the programme opening, and the last date to apply is set as Aug 15. âA student can apply for multiple Indian Army internship opportunities, but a student can accept only one internship offer letter. Before accepting an offer letter, ensure it is the opportunity that best matches studentâs skills, interests, and career aspirations,â the AICTE website said.

World.title: MP Parimal Nathwani urges Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren to resolve students' demands through dialogue following lathi charge
World.content:
Parimal Nathwani urged CM Soren to have talks with students

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A day after the student protestors were lathi-charged in Jharkhand during the 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march, Independent MP Parimal Nathwurged Chief Minister Hemant Soren to sympathetically address student protests over alleged JPSC and JSSC irregularities, emphasising that constructive dialogue is the best path to a resolution.Taking to X, Nathwani posted, "Earnestly request Hon'ble CM Shri Hemant Soren and the Jharkhand government to sympathetically consider the demands of the students. I strongly believe that a peaceful resolution through dialogue is the best way forward to protect the aspirations of our young candidates."The ongoing agitation has largely centred on demands raised by aspirants of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC). Protesters have been demanding cancellation of the JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process.Speaking to ANI outside Parliament, Nathwani earlier elaborated on the situation, noting that the state administration has already agreed to a significant portion of the protesters' grievances."The state government has already met about 80% of their demands. The CM should have looked into the remaining key issues," he said.Pushing for dialogue after the escalation of protests, he added, "As for the students, they went to the CM's residence and then to the Legislative Assembly; the lathi-charge that occurred was truly unfortunate. I would urge Hemant Soren to sit down with them immediately and find a way forward."Nathwani expressed solidarity with their youth's plight while cautioning against unrest. "Your issues are significant, and we stand with you regarding what you have endured, but a resolution will only come through dialogue," he stated.His remarks come after police resorted to a lathi charge on Monday evening to disperse students protesting outside the Jharkhand Assembly in Ranchi. Demonstrators vowed to continue their agitation over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations and demanded a CBI probe.Authorities deployed tear gas shells, water cannons, and lathi charges as a large number of aspirants attempted to move toward the Assembly.Meanwhile, Jharkhand Minister Deepika Pandey Singh earlier said the government had been engaging with the protesters and maintained that the administration had been instructed to maintain law and order."In a democracy, there is permission for protests; people are free to hold them. The administration is taking the necessary actions to maintain law and order. There will be no use of pellet guns, tear gas, or lathi-charge here," she said.On allegations of a communication gap, the minister said, "It wasn't a lack of communication; we held discussions for hours--talks have been ongoing for four days. We agreed to everything that was within the state government's capacity to address."She said cancellation of the CGL examination involved legal considerations. "The issue they are adamant about cancelling the CGL exam- involves judicial directives. The students should understand that the state government must operate within the framework of constitutional rights and established guidelines. We have accepted nearly every point," Pandey Singh added.She said the government was open to investigations into alleged financial irregularities."We have kept the investigation open-ended; the state government is ready to have the probe conducted under judicial monitoring. We have even invited the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to investigate the allegations of financial misappropriation," she said.

World.title: Two life convicts challenge sentences in 2020 IB officer Ankit Sharma murder case
World.content:
Two men sentenced to life imprisonment have challenged their conviction and sentence before the higher court.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

'No connection at all with Tahir'

NEW DELHI: Two men sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) official Ankit Sharma during the 2020 North East Delhi riots have challenged their conviction and sentence before the higher court.The convicts, Nazim and Kasim, were among five people convicted by the Karkardooma court in Delhi in the murder case. The court convicted them and three others, including former MCD councillor Tahir Hussain, on July 13 and sentenced them to life imprisonment on July 31.Speaking to ANI earlier, Mohammad Asif, the brother of convicts Nazim and Kasim, claimed that his brothers had been falsely implicated in the case and denied any connection with Tahir Hussain."We will appeal in the High Court. One of my brothers, the younger one, Kasim, lived in the village. The other one too had gone to the village two days before the incident. Tahir Hussain's house is very far away; we had no connection at all," Asif said.Sharma, an IB official, was killed during the communal violence that broke out in North East Delhi in February 2020. His body was later recovered from a drain in the Dayal Pur area.

World.title: Climate change, human activity driving Himalayan extreme weather, Centre tells Lok Sabha
World.content:
Climate change and human activity are making extreme rainfall events and disasters in the Himalayan region more frequent and intense, Centre at Lok Sabha.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Climate change is making extreme rainfall events in the Himalayan region more frequent and intense, while human activity is also increasing the risk of disasters, the Centre told the Lok Sabha on Tuesday, as reported by news agency PTI.Minister of state for home affairs Nityanand Rai said assessments by weather experts, scientific institutions and state authorities had found a link between climate change and the worsening intensity and frequency of extreme rainfall events in the Himalayas.The response came to a question on whether climate change and unscientific construction were contributing to the rising incidence of cloudbursts and other disasters in Himachal Pradesh.Rai cited findings of a Multi-Sectoral Central Team (MSCT), which was formed to examine the increasing frequency and severity of cloudbursts, flash floods, landslides and extreme rainfall in the state. The team includes experts from the National Disaster Management Authority, Central Building Research Institute, Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, IIT Indore and other agencies.Inputs from the India Meteorological Department, Central Water Commission and Geological Survey of India have also been considered as part of the assessment.The MSCT is examining the causes behind the increase in extreme weather events, including the geographical and ground conditions of the worst-hit areas and data provided by various government agencies. It will also recommend long-term steps to reduce the impact of such disasters, Rai said.The Centre said faster snowmelt was another factor contributing to increased runoff in high-altitude areas. Rapid melting can send large volumes of water into already vulnerable mountain terrain, increasing downstream flows.The government also flagged moraine instability as a factor behind off-season slope failures and heavy runoff. Moraines are deposits of loose rock, soil and other debris left behind by glaciers, which can become unstable and trigger slope failures and the movement of water and debris.

World.title: No Chinese encroachment in Arunachal, social media claims 'attention-seeking ploy': Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: There is no âslow encroachmentâ by China into Arunachal Pradesh, new agency ANI reported citing sources on Tuesday. The sources also rejected claims circulating on social media, describing them as âattention-seeking ploysâ that lack specific evidence.

"There is no slow encroachment in Arunachal Pradesh by China as alleged," they said.

"Due to undemarcated border at times the patrols face off each other, this is resolved through existing mechanisms and protocols in vogue. The Army and ITBP are geared up to dominate the border, monitor and check Chinese activities. Sensational claims like this without going into specifics are attention-seeking ploys," the report said citing sources.

They said China has historically laid claim to Arunachal Pradesh, referring to it as âSouth Tibetâ. During the 1960 border talks, Beijing had claimed around 69,000 sq km of territory in the state.

Also read |

â "China has claims on Arunachal as South Tibet, articulated in 1960 border talks, wherein they claimed approx 69,000 sq km of the state territory. â In 1959 China attacked the Assam Rifles outpost at Longju and captured it.





The area has since been in adverse possession and is frequently in news due to infra development done in this area by China," they said.

"During 1962 India-China War, major Chinese operations were launched in Kameng, Subansiri, Siyom, Siang and Lohit valleys. However, after ceasefire the PLA went back North of the LAC. Arunachal Pradesh shares a large border with Tibet along Great Himalayan range. Concerted infra push in recent years has enabled enhanced ptlg and surveillance of the area," they added.

The report comes after the ministry of external affairs (MEA) reiterated that Arunachal Pradesh is an "inalienable and integral part of India", referring to the recent "objection" by China over renaming places in the state.

World.title: CM Vijay likely to move resolution in Assembly seeking freeze on Lok Sabha seats at 543
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay is expected to move a resolution in the Assembly on Wednesday (August 11, 2026) regarding the proposed delimitation exercise, urging the Union government to permanently maintain the existing strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 and retain the current inter-State distribution of seats.

Editorial | Case for consensus: On delimitation

Mr. Vijay had, on August 8, 2026, convened a meeting with Members of Parliament from Tamil Nadu at Kalaivanar Arangam in Chennai. Of the total 57 MPs — 39 in the Lok Sabha and 18 in the Rajya Sabha — from Tamil Nadu, only 19 MPs participated. At the meeting, it was decided to adopt a resolution in the Assembly to protect the rights of Tamil Nadu and the southern States.

The resolution is also likely to emphasise maintaining the current Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha ratio of 2.2:1, while simultaneously implementing 33% reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha and subsequent Assembly elections without any delay, based on the existing 543 seats.
